recipes.title: Easy ONE POT CHORIZO Pasta
ingredients: Chicken or vegetable stock — 500 ml (2 cups)
Tin of finely chopped tomatoes — 400 g (14 oz)
steps: Brown the chorizo: Heat the olive oil and fry the chorizo in a single layer until coloured on both sides and some of its oil has rendered out (it can smoke). Remove it.
Soften the aromatics: In the chorizo oil, cook the onion and garlic for a couple of minutes with a little salt and a good amount of pepper.
Add peppers and paprika: Add the peppers and cook a little, then stir in the smoked paprika.
Add pasta and sauce: Stir in the dried pasta, then the tinned tomatoes, oregano, thyme, tomato paste, sugar and stock.
Simmer: Bring to the boil, cover and simmer about 10 minutes, stirring now and then so nothing sticks. Add a little water if it gets too dry; you want a thickish tomato sauce.
Add cheese and cream: Add torn mozzarella and some Parmesan, let it melt a little, then stir in the cream and the chopped spinach to wilt.
Return the chorizo: Add the chorizo and its juices back, let it bubble briefly and stir through with some fresh parsley.
Serve: Serve with a little Parmesan and fresh parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ddugVuQfHy8

recipes.title: GREEK Yoghurt CAESAR Salad and Croutons
ingredients: Fat-free Greek yogurt — ½ cup (a 240 ml carton in the video)
Parmesan, very finely grated — 1½ tbsp (plus more to taste)
Sugar — about 1 tsp (added in the video to taste)
Bacon — 3 slices, cooked crisp and crumbled
Grated Parmesan — ¼ cup, for garnish
Old bread, cut into 1 in cubes
Olive oil and melted salted butter
Seasoning powder of choice (garlic, onion, etc.)
steps: Make the croutons: Cut the bread into 1 in cubes (crusts off if you like). Toss with olive oil, a little melted salted butter, oregano, a little thyme and any seasoning powder.

Toast: Spread on baking trays and toast in a moderate oven for about 15 minutes, turning and swapping trays, until crisp. Leave the door open briefly to let them steam off. They keep in an airtight container.
Crisp the bacon: Dry fry the bacon in a pan, using its own fat, until crisp. Cool, then chop small.

Make the dressing: Mix the yogurt with Parmesan, Worcestershire sauce, black pepper, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, olive oil and pressed garlic. Taste, add about a teaspoon of sugar and a bit more Parmesan.
Assemble: Put the romaine (1–2 in pieces) in a bowl, add the bacon bits, croutons and grated Parmesan, then the dressing, and toss. Top with more Parmesan and dressing.
Variations and storage: For vegetarian, leave out the bacon and use soy sauce instead of Worcestershire. Keep leftover dressing in the fridge and use within about a week.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t62128OaDu0
Uploaded 2024-04-18.

recipes.title: Creamy CHICKEN SUPREME
ingredients: Boneless chicken breasts, skin on or skinless — 2–4
Olive oil — 1 tbsp (about 4 tbsp used in the video)
Salt and freshly ground black pepper — to taste
White wine — ½ cup (120 ml), optional
Cream — ½ cup (120 ml), or as much as you like
steps: Prep: Dice the onion, smash and chop the garlic, chop the parsley and slice the mushrooms.
Season and dust: Season the chicken on both sides with salt and pepper, then dust lightly with flour.

Brown the chicken: Heat the olive oil and butter, add the chicken skin side down over moderate heat and brown well, flipping two or three times and turning onto the sides if thick, until coloured. Remove to rest.
Soften the aromatics: Add the garlic and onions to the pan with a pinch of dried thyme, then the mushrooms, letting them soak up the butter and oil. Season with pepper and a little salt.
Deglaze: Add the white wine (or just use chicken stock) and cook down briefly.
Make the sauce: Add some parsley, the chicken stock and cream.
Finish the chicken: Return the chicken to the pan, turn the heat down and cook until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened a little. Season with pepper.
Serve: Serve with parsley stirred in or scattered over.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UkhGZ_gASpo

recipes.title: Lamb & Mint Pie
ingredients: Beef stock made with a cube — 1 cup, to rehydrate the soy protein
Beef broth made from granules — 2 cups
steps: Rehydrate the soy: Break up the soy chunks to mince-sized pieces and soak them in the beef stock (made with a cube) for about 15 minutes.
Make the pastry: Rub the butter and shortening into the flour and salt, then mix in the egg beaten with the water and vinegar and bring together. Cover and set aside.
Cook the lamb: Heat a little oil and butter, add the onion, garlic, rosemary, thyme, black pepper and salt, then the lamb mince. Break it up and cook it gently so the fat renders out.
Add the soy and seasoning: Stir in the rehydrated soy protein and cook it in the lamb juices. Add the Worcestershire sauce and tomato paste.
Mint, peas and gravy: Stir in 1 tbsp mint sauce, taste, then add a second. Add the frozen peas and the beef gravy and cook uncovered until thick. Taste for seasoning, then cool a little.
Line the tin: Roll out the base pastry, line the base of the 9 in springform tin, and ease the pastry in, trimming a little overhang. Preheat the oven/air fryer to 180°C.
Lid: Roll a top, lay it over the filling, tuck it in, trim, then twist and crimp the edge inside the tin. Add a simple pattern, brush with egg wash and cut a few vents.
Bake: Bake about 25 minutes until golden. Rest about 10 minutes before releasing from the tin and slicing.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JKZXCaClE9w
Uploaded 2024-04-16.

recipes.title: Tortilla VERDE con Queso TRADITIONAL Tortilla TWIST
ingredients: Milk — ¼ cup or a good splash
Medium potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced — 4–5
Cabbage, thinly sliced — ½ head (a whole small one in the video)
Dried thyme — 1 tsp (a pinch in the video)
Olive oil — for cooking (about 3 tbsp for the tortilla)
Cheese (cheddar and mozzarella in the video) — as much as you like
steps: Par-boil the potatoes: Thinly slice the potatoes, put them in a pan of salted water, bring to the boil, give them 5 minutes, then turn off. Drain and cool.

Sauté the veg: Remove the cabbage stalk and slice the cabbage very thinly. Cook it in olive oil and a little butter with the thinly sliced onion and the garlic, a pinch of thyme, a little salt and pepper (and smoked paprika if you like), stirring until wilted and the moisture cooks out. Cool slightly.
Make the egg mix: Lightly beat the eggs with black pepper and salt, add the milk, and stir in cheddar and mozzarella.
Combine: Stir in the cabbage mixture, then gently fold in the potatoes without mashing them.

Cook: Heat about 3 tbsp olive oil in a pan over low heat, add half the mixture, scatter over more cheese, then add the rest. Cover and cook slowly, now and then running a spatula around the edge and drawing it in, until thickened like a thick omelette.
Flip: Turn off the heat, cover with a plate, flip, and slide back into the pan. Cook uncovered over low heat for a couple of minutes to colour and set the other side.
Serve: Sprinkle with parsley and serve warm or cold, in slices, as a main or side.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sNViJzHr0eM

recipes.title: Red Lentil Bolognese
ingredients: Celery stalks, finely chopped — 2 (listed in the description)
Mushrooms, thickly sliced — used in the video (amount not stated)
Crushed tomatoes — 2 cups (tinned tomatoes chopped in the tin in the video)
Nutritional yeast bolognese seasoning mix — 2 tbsp (optional, below)
Tomato paste — 1 tbsp (2 tbsp in the video)
Sugar — about ½ tbsp (used in the video)
Smoked paprika — a little (used in the video)
Salt and black pepper — to taste
Olive oil — 2 tbsp (plus a little butter in the video)
Pasta of your choice — for serving
steps: Prep the veg: Dice the onion, smash and chop the garlic, and dice the carrots and pepper. Slice the mushrooms fairly thick.
Sauté: Heat a little butter and olive oil, add the onion and garlic with a good pinch of dried oregano, a little salt and pepper, and sauté briefly.
Add the mushrooms and veg: Add the mushrooms and let them soak up the fat, then add the pepper and carrots, the seasoning mix and a little smoked paprika. Stir fry a minute or so.
Add the tomatoes: Add the tomatoes (chopped in the tin with scissors if whole), the tomato paste and about ½ tbsp sugar to balance the acidity.
Add lentils and stock: Stir in the red lentils (rinsed if you like) and the vegetable stock gently.
Simmer: Bring to a simmer, cover and cook about 25 minutes, stirring now and then so nothing sticks and topping up with water if needed, until the lentils are done.
Thicken: Uncover and cook, stirring, until thick.
Add basil: Stir in freshly chopped basil for the last couple of minutes, keeping some for garnish.
Serve: Cook the spaghetti in salted boiling water as per the packet and serve with the sauce and basil.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8B3AQwN0WDA
Uploaded 2024-04-14.

recipes.title: Shepherd's Pie An Englishman’s Recipe @HYSapientia
ingredients: Beef broth made from granules or a cube — 2 cups
Frozen mixed vegetables — 1 cup (or 1 celery stick, diced, 1 carrot, diced, and 1 cup frozen peas, as in the video)
Potatoes, peeled and diced — 2 lb (1 kg)
steps: Boil the potatoes: Put the potatoes on to boil in salted water.
Start the filling: Melt the butter in a pan with the diced onion and garlic. Add a little salt (the gravy granules are salty).
Cook the lamb: Add the lamb with a good pinch of dried thyme (and rosemary) and some pepper, and cook it down together with the onions. Stir in about 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce.
Add the hard veg: Add the diced celery and carrot and cook, stirring, to soften.
Add tomato and gravy: Stir in the tomato paste and cook it in, then add the frozen peas and the beef broth.
Thicken: Simmer, stirring now and then, until the veg is tender and the gravy has thickened but isn't dry. Turn off the heat.
Mash: Drain the potatoes, dry them on the heat with a shake, then mash with butter and a splash of milk. Preheat the oven to 190°C (air fryer 180°C).
Assemble: Spread the meat in a dish, top with the mash, bring it to the edges with a fork, and rough up the surface into peaks. Season the top lightly and add cheddar if you like.
Bake: Bake about 20 minutes until browned and crusted.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AlujpU0azmo
Uploaded 2024-04-13.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 380°F (190°C) – 20  mins cook; Air fryer 360°F (180°C)  – 20  mins coo.

recipes.title: How to Make CREAMY MUSHROOM RISOTTO like an Italian not by an Italian
ingredients: Fresh mushrooms (cremini or button), thickly sliced — 1 lb
Vegetable broth (or broth of choice), warm — 6 cups (about 900 ml)
Olive oil — 2 tbsp (about 3 tbsp for the rice in the video)
Salt and black pepper — to taste
Fresh parsley, chopped — for cooking and garnish
steps: Prep: Dice the onion very finely (about the size of the rice grains), mince the garlic, mince some parsley, and slice the wiped mushrooms thickly.

Cook the mushrooms: Heat olive oil and a little butter in a wide pan, add the mushrooms with a little salt and pepper, and cook gently until they absorb the fat, release their juices and take on some colour. Add a little parsley. Set aside.
Sweat the aromatics: Heat about 3 tbsp olive oil and sweat the onion and garlic over low to medium heat until soft and translucent, with no colour.
Toast the rice: Add the rice and stir gently for a minute to toast.
Add wine: Pour in the wine and cook until it has evaporated.

Add stock gradually: Add warm stock a little at a time, cooking slowly and stirring enough to prevent sticking, letting each addition absorb before the next. This takes up to about 25 minutes; use water if you run out of stock.
Check: Taste for seasoning and doneness; the rice should be creamy with a little firmness in the middle.
Finish: Stir in parsley (keeping some back), the Parmesan, then the butter. Loosen with a little more stock or water, since it thickens as it stands.
Add the mushrooms: Stir in most of the mushrooms and warm through for a couple of minutes.
Serve: Top with the remaining mushrooms, a little Parmesan and parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5zkZBV1vxNg
Uploaded 2024-04-12.

recipes.title: Pesto NO Pine Nuts -  Pesto Pasta
ingredients: Ground almonds (or substitute, such as soaked cashews) — ½ cup
Lemon juice — juice of ½ lemon
Pasta of choice (spaghetti in the video), cooked to packet instructions
Any topping of choice (sun-dried tomatoes in the video)
steps: Blend the pesto: Put the ground almonds, basil, salt, black pepper, lemon juice, Parmesan and garlic in a blender with some olive oil and blend, drizzling in more oil (and shaking or scraping down as needed) until smooth and vibrant green. Taste.
Store any extra: Spoon spare pesto into a jar and seal the top with a layer of olive oil to stop it darkening. Refrigerate and use while fresh; top up the oil after each use.
Cook the pasta: Cook the pasta in salted boiling water (no oil) to the packet instructions. Keep some starchy pasta water.
Combine: Lift the pasta straight into a bowl with a little water clinging to it, add the pesto and a splash of pasta water, and toss to coat.
Serve: Serve topped with Parmesan and any topping you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JoAd3c_ySpw

recipes.title: Apple Turnovers Using Ready-Made Puff Pastry
ingredients: Ready-made puff pastry, thawed — 1 package (about 17.3 oz)
Medium green (Granny Smith) apples, peeled, cored and diced — 4–5
Medium sweet eating apples, peeled, cored and diced — 2
Granulated sugar — ¼ cup (50 g) (about 1 tbsp in the video, plus a little for sprinkling)
Cornflour — 1 tbsp, mixed with a little water
Or mixed spice — instead of the cinnamon and nutmeg
Egg white, beaten — 1, for the glaze
Powdered sugar — ¼ cup (30 g), optional, for dusting
steps: Prep the apples: Put a splash of water and some lemon juice in the pan. Peel, core and finely cube the green apples straight into it, turning them to stop browning. Cube the eating apples into a separate bowl with a little lemon juice.
Cook the green apples: Over the heat, add the sugar, about 1 tbsp lemon juice, a little salt and the spice, and cook about 10 minutes until very soft and mushy.
Add the eating apples: Stir them in and cook about 5 minutes to soften while keeping some crunch. Add water if it gets too dry.
Thicken: Stir in the cornflour slurry until thick and glossy. Turn off the heat and let it cool completely (it firms as it cools).
Cut the pastry: Cut the puff pastry into roughly six squares.
Fill and fold: Spoon filling (including chunky apple) toward one corner, brush the edges with egg white, fold over into a triangle and press down. Crimp the edges with a floured fork.
Finish: Put on a tray, cut three slits in each top, brush lightly with egg white, and sprinkle with a little sugar.
Bake: Bake at 175–190°C for about 15–20 minutes (description: oven 180°C/360°F or air fryer 170°C/340°F) until golden.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bxXFvRyPqa4
Uploaded 2024-04-10.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 360°F (180°C)  15–20  mins; Air fryer 340°F (170°C)  15–20 mins.

recipes.title: CHORLEY Cakes Traditional LANCASHIRE Affectionately FLY PIE @HYSapientia
ingredients: Milk or beaten egg white — for glazing
A little extra caster sugar — very optional
Lancashire cheese or sharp cheddar — to serve
steps: Make the pastry: Rub the butter and shortening into the flour, salt and sugar to fine breadcrumbs. Beat the egg with the water and vinegar, stir it in with a fork handle, then bring together gently by hand.
Make the filling: Mix the currants with the sugar and melted butter.
Preheat: Heat the oven to 190–200°C (air fryer 180°C).
Cut rounds: Roll the pastry out and cut rounds (a 6 in cutter in the video; traditionally about 4 in). Re-roll the scraps to make more.

Fill and shape: Put a deep layer of filling in the middle of each round, wet the edge with a little water, pull the edges up to the centre and pinch to seal. Turn over and roll gently into a flat round about 4 in across.
Finish: Put on a lined tray, cut three slits in the top, and brush with milk (traditionally no sugar on top).
Bake: Bake about 15 minutes (description: 15–20 minutes) until lightly golden.
Serve: Serve with a slice of Lancashire cheese or sharp cheddar.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gvxdlqj6GaE
Uploaded 2024-04-09.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 380°F (190°C)  15–20  mins; Air fryer 360°F (180°C)  15–20 mins.

recipes.title: SOUTHERN-Style Black eyed peas Hoppin' John
ingredients: Dried black-eyed peas, soaked overnight and drained — 1 lb (500 g)
Smoked ham hock (or 2 cups diced ham) — 1 (a lump of bacon cut into chunks in the video)
Bacon rashers, cubed and fried crispy — 5–6
Salt — to taste (depends on the broth and bacon)
White rice and cornbread — to serve
steps: Start the peas: Rinse the soaked peas and put them in a large pan with the bay leaf and chicken broth. Bring to the boil, adding more liquid if needed.
Prep: Chop the garlic and onion; dice the carrots, celery, green pepper and jalapeños. Cut the bacon lump into good chunks and slice the rashers.
Fry the bacon: In a pan with a little butter, fry the sliced rashers until crispy and remove, leaving the fat. Then brown the bacon chunks lightly to render fat (not too long) and remove them too.
Sweat and bloom: Sweat the garlic and onions in the bacon fat, then add the black pepper, Creole seasoning, cayenne and smoked paprika to bloom in the oil.
Coat the veg: Stir in the remaining vegetables to coat, then add the apple cider vinegar.
Simmer: Tip everything from the pan into the peas, cover and simmer for about 1 hour. Add the bacon chunks/ham and cook about another half hour.
Thicken: Mash a couple of spoonfuls of peas against the side and stir back in. Stir in some crispy bacon and a little of the bacon fat and warm through.
Serve: Serve over white rice with cornbread, topped with crispy bacon and parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TmAo6gVk6i4
Uploaded 2024-04-08.

recipes.title: WET Nelly LIVERPOOL Traditional Dessert
ingredients: Leftover bread, torn into pieces (crusts optional) — 10 oz (about 300 g)
Milk — 2 cups (480 ml) (1 can evaporated milk plus milk in the video)
Unsalted butter, melted — ¼ cup (50 g), plus extra for the dish
Vanilla — a little (used in the video)
Mixed dried fruit (raisins, sultanas, currants) — 1 cup (150 g), soaked 4 hours in rum and water in the video
Orange peel — a little (optional, used in the video)
Chopped nuts — ¼ cup (50 g), optional
steps: Preheat: Heat the oven to about 175–180°C (360°F).
Soak the bread: Cut or tear the bread into small pieces in a bowl. Pour in the evaporated milk, then more milk, and let the bread absorb it.
Mix: Add the beaten eggs, melted butter, vanilla, sugar, mixed spice, soaked fruit, orange peel, lemon zest and rum if using. Mix to a wet mixture.
Fill the dish: Butter an 8 × 8 in dish, set it on a tray and drop the mixture in without squashing it, leaving peaks to crust over.

Bake: Bake until a knife comes out clean. The description corrects the video's 35–40 minutes: oven 180°C for about 20 minutes, air fryer 175°C for about 14 minutes. Cover with foil if it browns too fast.
Make the custard: In a pan, mix milk, the sugar, a little vanilla, the cornflour and a little yellow colouring. Heat gently, stirring, to the boil until thickened. Thin with milk if too thick.
Serve: Cut into squares and serve with the custard.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CQJgl8e83Ww
Uploaded 2024-04-07.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 380°F (180°C)  20 mins.

recipes.title: MARRY ME Chicken
ingredients: Boneless chicken breasts or thighs (skinless, or skin-on thighs as in the video) — 2
Red chilli flakes — 1 tsp (adjust to taste)
Chicken broth (made with a cube) — 1 cup
Shredded spinach (frozen, defrosted, in the video) — 1 cup
Fresh thyme, chopped — 1 tsp (dried in the video)
Fresh oregano, chopped — 1 tsp (dried in the video)
steps: Season and dust: If using breasts, butterfly them into two pieces. Season both sides with black pepper, salt and smoked paprika, then lightly dust with flour.
Brown: Heat butter and olive oil and brown the chicken skin side down until crisp, then turn and cook the other side a little. Remove to a tray.
Sauté the aromatics: In the pan juices, sauté the onion and garlic with a good pinch of oregano and a little thyme until just tinged.
Tomato and mustard: Stir in the tomato paste and cook it in, then add about 1 tsp Dijon mustard.
Build the sauce: Add the chicken broth, then the spinach, the sun-dried tomatoes and the chilli flakes.
Add cream and zest: Stir in a good dollop of cream (more if needed) and a little lemon zest, and warm through without boiling hard.
Cheese and chicken: Stir in the Parmesan, return the chicken and its juices, add some chopped basil, and warm the chicken through, reducing the sauce if you want it thicker.
Serve: Serve with extra Parmesan and basil.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ueB1ACZoZOM
Uploaded 2024-04-06.

recipes.title: BEEF Mushroom STOUT Pie
ingredients: Olive oil — 2 tbsp (plus a little butter in the video)
Beef chuck, cut into 1 in cubes — 1 kg (about 2.2 lb)
Salt and black pepper — to taste
Tomato paste — 2 tbsp (about 1 tbsp in the video)
Stout beer (such as Guinness) — 1 bottle (about 12 oz)
Beef broth — 2 cups (stock cubes in the video)
Cornflour — 1 tbsp mixed with 2 tbsp water (used in the video)
steps: Start the base: Heat the oil and a little butter and add the onions and garlic with black pepper and a good amount of dried thyme (no salt; the stock is salty).
Sear the beef: Add the beef and give it a little colour if you can.
Add flavourings: Stir in about 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, the tomato paste and about 2 tbsp flour.

Add liquid and simmer: Pour in the stout and the stock, stir, cover and simmer gently, stirring now and then so it doesn't stick, for about 1 hour 10 minutes to 1½ hours, until a fork goes in with a little resistance.
Add the mushrooms: Stir in the thick-cut mushrooms, cover and cook about 20 minutes more.
Thicken: Spoon off some gravy and keep it. Stir in the cornflour slurry until thickish (add water or the reserved gravy if it gets too thick). Cool.

Make the pastry: Rub the shortening and butter into the flour and salt to breadcrumbs. Beat the egg with the water and vinegar, stir in with a fork handle and bring together. Use half and wrap the rest for another time.

Assemble: Roll out and line a 9 in springform tin with overhang. Add the filling plus a little reserved gravy, wet the edge, lay on the rolled lid, tuck it inside and fold the overhang over. Crimp with your fingers.
Bake: Bake at 190°C (air fryer 180°C) for about 35 minutes until golden.

From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OABG1sJuNjY
Uploaded 2024-04-05.

recipes.title: Corned BEEF LASAGNA  Deliciously A Purists NIGHTMARE!
ingredients: Tinned corned beef, crumbled — 2 cans (340 g each)
Lasagna noodles/sheets, cooked to package instructions — 9
Salt and pepper — to taste (no salt in the video; corned beef is salty)
steps: Make the tomato sauce: Sauté the onion and garlic in olive oil or butter with a good pinch of dried oregano. Add the juice from the tin of tomatoes, then the chopped tomatoes, the tomato purée and the pasta sauce, and warm until slightly thickened. Turn off the heat.
Add the corned beef: Mash the corned beef and stir it gently through the sauce, keeping some lumps for texture.

Béchamel, traditional: Melt the butter over moderate heat, stir in the flour and cook out the rawness, then add milk a little at a time, switching to a whisk, until smooth and as thick as you like. Add a pinch of nutmeg.

Béchamel, quick: Warm milk in a pan, stir in the cornflour until dissolved, and keep stirring as it comes up to the boil and thickens. Turn off the heat, stir in a knob of butter and a pinch of nutmeg. (The video combines both batches.)
Layer: Spread some béchamel in the dish, then a layer of lasagna sheets, the meat sauce, more béchamel and a little cheese. Repeat, finishing with sheets and a mozzarella top.
Bake: Cover with foil and bake at 180–190°C for 25 minutes. Uncover and bake about 10–15 minutes more (the description gives 9 minutes uncovered in the air fryer) until bubbling and lightly browned.
Serve: Let it cool a little before cutting.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sHP0VFceq3E
Uploaded 2024-04-04.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C). cook 25 mins covered 10 -15 mins uncovered; Air fryer 360°F (180°C). cook 25 mins covered 9 mins uncovered.

recipes.title: Tomato SOUP QUICHE Inspired Recipe
ingredients: Condensed tomato soup (Campbell's in the video) — 1 can (10.75 oz)
Onion (red in the video), finely diced — ½ cup (about half an onion)
Fresh basil, finely chopped — ½ cup, or 2 tbsp basil pesto
Optional garnish: fresh basil, parsley, Parmesan
Beaten egg — for the glaze seal
steps: Make the pastry: Rub the fats into the flour and salt, then stir in the egg beaten with the water and vinegar and bring together. Wrap and set aside.
Sauté the onion: Gently sauté the diced onion in a little butter, then let it cool.
Mix the filling: Beat the eggs with pepper and a little salt, then stir in the tomato soup, cream and pesto (or chopped basil). Add the onions and cheddar.
Line the tin: Preheat to 180–190°C. Butter a 9 in loose-bottom tin, roll the pastry out (it's soft, so handle with care), line the tin with some overhang, and dock the base with a fork.
Blind bake: Line with parchment and baking beads and bake about 15 minutes. Remove the beads, brush the base with beaten egg and bake about 3 minutes more to seal.
Fill and bake: Trim the crust, pour in the filling, lower the heat to 160–180°C and bake about 30–35 minutes until set.
Rest and serve: Let it settle about 10 minutes, remove from the tin, and finish with grated Parmesan and chopped parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZyhZ_7IU9JA
Uploaded 2024-04-03.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 380°F (190°C)  15 mins – seal 3 mins –; Air fryer 360°F (180°C)  15 mins – seal 3 mins –.

recipes.title: WELSH PLATE CAKE  Teisen Lap Traditional WELSH cake @HYSapientia
ingredients: Unsalted butter, room temperature — 110 g (4 oz)
Mixed dried fruit (raisins, sultanas, currants) — 110 g (4 oz), soaked in a cup of tea in the video (optional)
Mixed spice — 1 tsp (or cinnamon, nutmeg and allspice)
Lemon zest — of 1 lemon (just a little in the video)
steps: Prep: Line a shallow 8 in cake tin. If you like, soak the dried fruit in a cup of tea beforehand and drain.
Cream: Cream the butter and sugar, then add the beaten egg with a little of the flour to stop it curdling.
Make the batter: Put the rest of the flour in a bowl with a pinch of salt, add the egg mixture and the mixed spice, and mix, adding the milk gradually to make a batter.
Add fruit and zest: Stir in the fruit and a little lemon zest.

Bake: Pour into the tin and tap to level. Bake at 180°C (350°F) (air fryer about 170–175°C) for about 35 minutes, up to 45 in an oven, covering with foil if the top browns too fast, until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool: Cool before slicing.
recipes.notes:

Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 360°F (180°C) – 35 - 45 mins cook; Air fryer 350°F (175°C)  – 35 mins cook.

recipes.title: Chicken and Leek RISOTTO EASY Cook Recipe
ingredients: Butter — 2 tbsp, divided (optional; use olive oil for a lighter dish)
Large chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces — 2
Salt and white (or black) pepper — to taste
Leeks, white and light green parts, thinly sliced — 2
steps: Cook the chicken: Heat a little butter and the olive oil over moderate heat, add the chicken with a little salt and white pepper, and cook until done. Remove to a bowl.
Soften the leeks: Add a little more butter, then the garlic and sliced leeks with a pinch of salt and white pepper, and stir fry until softened.
Toast the rice: Stir in the rice and cook 1–2 minutes until slightly translucent at the edges.
Add wine: Per the description, add the wine after the rice has toasted and cook until absorbed.
Add stock gradually: Add warm stock a ladle at a time, stirring and letting each absorb before the next, for about 15–18 minutes until creamy.
Return the chicken: With the last ladle of stock, add the chicken back and let it warm through.
Finish: Stir in a little lemon zest and a small squeeze of lemon (not too much), check seasoning, then stir in chopped parsley and grated Parmesan.
Serve: Serve with a little extra Parmesan on top.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j816wTtI1jo
Uploaded 2024-04-01.

recipes.title: STEAK Bake COMFORTING Savoury Pastry
ingredients: Store-bought puff pastry, cut into 4.5 × 5 in pieces
Beef stock cubes — 2, in about 900 ml water
Salt and pepper — to taste (none used; the stock cubes are salty)
steps: Start the onions: Heat butter and a little oil and add the finely diced onion with about 1 tsp dried thyme.
Add the beef: Add the cubed beef and give it a little colour if you can.
Flavour: Stir in the Worcestershire sauce and about 1 tbsp tomato paste and cook briefly.
Simmer: Add the stock, bring to the boil, then cover and simmer about 1½–2 hours, stirring now and then, until fork-tender and the gravy is thick. If it cooks down too far, add water, not more stock.
Thicken and cool: Thicken further with a little cornflour slurry if needed (or cook uncovered). Pull apart any large cubes with a fork. Let the filling cool.
Preheat: Heat the oven to 180–190°C (air fryer about 175°C).
Fill: Pile filling onto a piece of pastry, brush the edges lightly with egg wash, lay another piece on top and press down to seal.
Mark: Crimp the edges with a fork, score diagonal lines across the top with a butter knife, and poke vent holes along the lines. Brush with egg wash.
Bake: Bake about 20 minutes until puffed and golden.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Gg8j52GvHWg
Uploaded 2024-03-31.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Cook about 1 ½ hours; oven to 360°F (180°C) – 20  mins cook; Air fryer 350°F (175°C)  – 20 mins cook.

recipes.title: PIEROGI Ruskie Traditional POLISH dumplings
ingredients: All-purpose/plain flour — 480 g (4 cups), plus extra for kneading and rolling
Cottage cheese or farmer's cheese, drained — 1 cup
Fried onion and butter (1 onion in the video)
Butter and a little oil — for pan-frying (optional)
steps: Boil and dry the potatoes: Boil the peeled potatoes until they take a fork, drain, and dry them in the pan over the heat.
Mash: Mash with salt, pepper and a little butter, leaving some texture. Let it go cold.
Finish the filling: Sauté the onion in butter until just tinged and mix into the potato. Crumble in the cottage cheese, season, and add a little chopped green onion if you like.
Make the dough: Mix the flour and salt, add the beaten egg, water and oil, and bring together. Knead on the counter to a slightly tacky dough. Cover and rest briefly (longer is better).
Shape: Roll the dough thin, cut rounds (4 in cutter per the description), add a spoonful of filling, fold over and pinch to seal.
Boil: Drop into boiling water; they sink, then float when cooked. Lift them into a tray with a little oil so they don't stick.
Make the topping: Fry an onion in plenty of butter, with a little salt and pepper if you like.
Pan-fry (optional): Fry the boiled pierogi in butter and a little oil over moderate heat until crisp and lightly charred.
Serve: Top with the buttery onions and a little green onion.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qzZTnis7aBw
Uploaded 2024-03-30.

recipes.title: SCOUSE LIVERPOOL’s OWN  | Slow Cooked SCOUSE
ingredients: Beef or lamb, or half and half (beef chuck and lamb shoulder in the video), cut into chunks — 1.5 lb (680 g)
Large potatoes, peeled and diced large — 4
Large carrots, peeled and cut into chunks — 2
Beef or vegetable broth (2 stock cubes in boiling water in the video) — 4 cups (950 ml)
Cornflour/cornstarch — 1 tbsp mixed with 1 tbsp water, to thicken
To serve: crusty bread, pickled red cabbage or beetroot
steps: Prep the veg and stock: Chop the onion and cut the carrots, swede and potatoes into decent chunks. Crumble the stock cubes into boiling water.
Season and flour the meat: Season the meat with salt, pepper and some dried thyme, then toss with a little flour.
Sear: Heat butter and oil over moderate heat and sear the meat all over for colour and a little crust. Put the meat into the slow cooker.
Deglaze: Put the pan back on the heat with a little of the stock and the onions, scrape up the sediment, then tip it all over the meat.
Layer: Add the swede, carrots and potatoes (and celery if using), the bay leaves, more thyme, about 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, and the rest of the broth.
Slow cook: Cover and cook on high for 4–5 hours (or low for 6–8 hours) until the meat is tender, stirring once or twice at most.
Thicken: Stir in the cornflour slurry for a slightly thicker gravy. Remove the bay leaves if you like.
Serve: Garnish with parsley and serve with crusty bread and pickled red cabbage or beetroot.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GmLOIOZ53bA
Uploaded 2024-03-29.

recipes.title: Meatless FRIDAY Savoury Cabbage, Potato, and Cheese Tart
ingredients: Pre-baked tart shell — 1 (9 in; an 8 in lined tin in the video), store-bought or homemade
Garlic — a couple of cloves (used in the video)
Large potato, thinly sliced (about ¼ in) — 1
Fresh thyme leaves — 1 tsp (or ½ tsp dried; a heaped tsp dried in the video)
Shredded cheese (Gruyère, cheddar or a mix) — 1 cup
steps: Blind bake the case: Line the tin with pastry, blind bake, and let it cool.
Blanch the potatoes: Thinly slice the potatoes into a pan of salted water and blanch for about 5 minutes. Drain and cool.
Sauté the veg: Melt the butter, add the thinly sliced onion and garlic, a good teaspoon of dried thyme, salt and pepper, then the thinly sliced cabbage. Sauté a couple of minutes until soft. Cool.
Make the custard: Beat the eggs and mix in about a cup of cream (and nutmeg if using).
Layer: Scatter a layer of cheese in the case, then cabbage mix, then a loose layer of potatoes. Pour on a little custard, then repeat the cabbage and potato layers.
Top: Add more cheese, pour over the rest of the custard to soak through, and finish with more cheese.
Bake: Bake at 190°C (air fryer 170°C) for about 22–30 minutes until the cheese has crusted over the top.
Serve: Let it cool a little and serve with anything you like, such as chips or beans.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lb6-0pMvtp8
Uploaded 2024-03-28.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 380°F (190°C) 25-30 mins; Air fryer 340°F (170°C)  22 -25 mins.

recipes.title: Barley Pudding SECOND COUSIN To Rice Pudding WHY?
ingredients: Pearl barley, rinsed and drained — 1 cup
Water — at least 2 cups, for the first cook
Whole milk — 2 cups, plus a little more if you like it saucy
Heavy cream — 1 cup, plus extra for serving
Raisins (golden and dark in the video) — 1 cup
steps: Simmer the barley: Put the barley in a pan with at least 2 cups of water, bring to the boil, turn down, cover and cook about 20–25 minutes, stirring now and then and checking the water so it doesn't stick or dry out, until plump and most of the liquid is absorbed.
Mix: Tip into a bowl and stir in the milk, cream, raisins, sugar, vanilla, salt and nutmeg.
Preheat and prep: Heat the oven to about 160–165°C (air fryer 140°C). Butter the baking dish.
Bake: Pour in the mixture and bake about 20–25 minutes, stirring the skin back in halfway, until it has a light golden crust.
Serve: Rest a couple of minutes and serve, with extra cream if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zBP-p0Y9_Hc
Uploaded 2024-03-27.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 320°F (160°C) 20 - 25 mins; Air fryer 280°F (140°C)  20 mins.

recipes.title: Yorkshire INSPIRED Minced BEEF and BARLEY Skillet
ingredients: Beef stock cube — a little, crumbled
Water — to cover the barley by about 1 cm, plus extra as needed
Mixed herbs (thyme, rosemary, sage) — 1 tsp (dried sage and thyme in the video)
Beef dripping or lard — for frying
To serve: mashed potatoes, onion gravy, parsley, English mustard
steps: Cook the barley: Put the barley in a pan with water to cover by about 1 cm and crumble in a little stock cube. Bring to the boil, then simmer about 30 minutes, stirring now and then and topping up with water so it doesn't dry out, until plump. Turn off and cool.

Mix: Finely dice the onion and add it to the mince with the herbs, nutmeg, salt, pepper and a splash of Worcestershire sauce. (If you don't like the onion less cooked, fry it first.) Mix in the barley thoroughly.
Fry: Heat lard in a skillet, add the mince mixture and fry, breaking it up gently (it may spit from the barley's moisture), until it picks up some colour but stays slightly moist.
Serve: Plate with mashed potato (stacked in rings if you like), top with the mince and barley, spoon over onion gravy, sprinkle with parsley, and add English mustard on the side.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fUtORp-nUiE

recipes.title: CHICKPEA and Cauliflower CURRY Pie with SWEET Potato Crust
ingredients: Large sweet potatoes (any colour), peeled and cubed — 3–4
Unsalted butter (vegan butter for vegan) — 2 tbsp
Butter/olive oil or oil of choice — 2 tbsp
Ginger, minced or cut into thin strips — 1 in piece
Cauliflower, cut into small florets — 1 head
Chickpeas, drained and rinsed — 1 can (15 oz)
Diced tomatoes — 1 can (14 oz) (whole tinned tomatoes crushed by hand in the video)
Chilli powder — ½–1 tsp (adjust to taste)
steps: Boil the sweet potatoes: Cube the sweet potatoes evenly and boil about 12–15 minutes until very soft.
Prep: Mash the garlic and cut the ginger into thin strips (or mince both).
Sauté: Melt the butter and cook the onion, garlic and ginger to release their aromatics (some colour is fine; don't burn).
Bloom the spices: Add the curry powder, garam masala, cumin and chilli powder and cook carefully in the little fat there is, without burning.
Crack the coconut milk: Push the onions aside, add some coconut milk and cook it down until it splits and releases its oil.
Build the curry: Add the chickpeas and a little more coconut milk, then the cauliflower and the tomatoes (crushed by hand or cut up), then the rest of the coconut milk.

Simmer: Bring to a simmer, cover and cook on low about 12–15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the cauliflower is fork-tender. Uncover for about a minute to thicken slightly, keeping plenty of sauce. Add cilantro if you like.
Mash: Drain the sweet potatoes, dry them on the heat, and mash with butter, a little salt and plenty of pepper.

Assemble and bake: Spread the curry in a baking dish, top with the mash and level it loosely, leaving it rough to crisp. Set on a tray and bake at 175–190°C for about 20–25 minutes until the top is crusty.
Serve: Garnish with cilantro.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=w0Eiv6iePXA
Uploaded 2024-03-25.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 380°F (190°C) 20 - 25 mins; Air fryer 360°F (180°C)  20 mins.

recipes.title: Apple STRUDEL - WHOLE APPLE Strudel
ingredients: Large apples, cored and hollowed out (flesh kept) — 2
Extra apple, peeled and cubed small — 1
Sweet mincemeat — 2 tbsp, or ¼ cup raisins (optional)
Brown sugar — ½ tbsp, or to taste
English mixed spice or pumpkin spice — 1 heaped tsp
To serve: squirty cream, whipped cream, vanilla ice cream or custard
steps: Hollow the apples: Cut the tops off the two large apples, remove the core, and scoop out the flesh with a melon baller or spoon, keeping the shells intact. Remove the bottom of the core so there's a hole right through.

Cook the filling: Melt the butter, add the scooped apple and the extra cubed apple with a little salt, and cook to soften (add a splash of water if needed). Stir in the sugar and mixed spice, then the mincemeat (or raisins). Cook about 7 minutes, then cool.
Cut the pastry: Unroll the puff pastry and cut a shape around each apple with tabs that are slightly wider at the ends so they fold into the top.
Wrap: Plug the hole in the base of each apple with a little piece of pastry, then wrap the pastry up the sides and tuck it over and inside the top, overlapping as you go.
Fill: Pack the filling into the apples right to the top.
Bake: Preheat to 180–190°C. Put the apples on a tray (no egg wash needed) and bake about 20–25 minutes until puffed and golden.
Serve: Serve with cream, ice cream or custard.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sckkc3mkyC0
Uploaded 2024-03-24.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 380°F (190°C) 20 - 25 mins; Air fryer 360°F (180°C)  20 mins.

recipes.title: Red lentil Shepherd's Pie with a Cauliflower Cheese Mash Crust
ingredients: Olive oil — 2 tbsp (butter in the video)
Red or green lentils, rinsed (or canned, drained) — 1 cup (220 g)
Cauliflower, cut into florets — 1 large head
Milk, cream or unsweetened almond milk — ¼ cup
Grated cheese (or vegan cheese) — ½ cup minimum, optional
steps: Boil the cauliflower: Boil the florets in salted water for about 12 minutes until very soft.

Cook the lentils: Put the lentils in a pan with the tomatoes (cut up if whole), tomato paste, veg stock, rosemary and thyme. Stir so they don't clump and simmer about 12–20 minutes, stirring often so they don't stick, until soft but with some texture.
Sauté the veg: In butter or oil, sauté the onion, garlic, carrots and celery for about 5 minutes until softening. Season with salt and pepper.
Add mushrooms and peas: Add the mushrooms and cook 5 minutes, then stir in the peas for a minute. Turn off the heat.
Combine: Mix the lentil mixture into the vegetables.
Make the mash: Drain the cauliflower well, return it to the pan with butter, pepper (and salt) and the cream, and mash, leaving some texture. Stir in cheese.
Assemble: Preheat the oven to about 180°C. Press the filling into a baking dish and top with the cauliflower mash, fluffing it up rather than squashing it, then sprinkle with more cheese.
Bake: Bake about 15–20 minutes (air fryer 170°C, 15 minutes) until browned and crispy on top.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UHRvNlN4iCY
Uploaded 2024-03-23.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 360°F (180°C) 15 mins; Air fryer 340°F (170°C)  15 mins.

recipes.title: Rumbledethumps CLASSIC SCOTTISH ULTIMATE Comfort dish
ingredients: Potatoes, peeled and cut into small chunks — 2 lb (about 900 g)
Cabbage (or a bunch of kale), sliced — 1 head
Milk or cream — ½ cup (about 120 ml)
Shredded cheddar (or any strong mature cheese) — 2 cups (about 200 g)
steps: Infuse the milk: Put the chopped green onions in a small pan with the milk and set aside.
Boil the potatoes: Boil the potato chunks (salted if you like) until they take a fork.

Sauté the cabbage: Remove the stalk and slice the cabbage. Melt a good amount of butter, sauté the onion with pepper, then add the cabbage in batches and cook until softened but with some texture. Take off the heat.
Warm the milk: Heat the milk with the green onions and more butter for a minute without burning, then set aside.
Mash: Drain the potatoes, dry them on the heat with a shake, then mash roughly with the infused milk and butter, keeping some lumps. Mix in just over half the cabbage.

Layer: In an 8 × 8 in dish, spoon in some mash, a layer of the remaining cabbage, a layer of cheese and black pepper (or mustard powder), then the rest of the mash piled up without compressing. Dot with any remaining cabbage and top with cheese.
Bake: Bake at 180°C (air fryer 170°C) for about 15–20 minutes until the cheese has melted and browned (or flash under the grill).
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P8j_-fbNO1k
Uploaded 2024-03-22.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 360°F (180°C) 15 - 20 mins; Air fryer 340°F (170°C)  15 mins.

recipes.title: HOT Cross Buns  PILLOW SOFT
ingredients: Plain/all-purpose or strong white bread flour — 500 g
Dried fruit/mixed peel (raisins and mixed peel in the video) — 300 g
steps: Mix the dry ingredients: In the mixer bowl, combine the flour, salt, sugar, yeast, mixed spice and cinnamon.
Add the wet: Add the water, egg and melted butter, and mix with the dough hook, slowly then faster, until it starts coming away from the sides (it stays very sticky).
Add the fruit: Mix in the dried fruit and peel on low, scraping down.
First rise: Tip into a lightly oiled bowl, cover and leave somewhere warm for about 1–1½ hours until doubled.
Knock back and second rise: With floured hands, knock the air out, return to the bowl, cover and let it rise again (about 30 minutes if warm).
Make the cross paste: Mix the flour, water and oil into a paste and put it in a piping bag.
Shape: Divide the dough into 100 g balls (12), roll each with lightly floured hands, and place in a 10 × 10 in tray. Cover and prove about 15 minutes. Preheat the oven to 190°C (air fryer 170°C).
Pipe and bake: Pipe continuous lines across each row both ways to make the crosses. Bake about 20–25 minutes (air fryer about 18).
Glaze: Warm the sugar and water into a syrup (or use apricot jam) and brush over the hot buns. Let stand about 10 minutes, then cool on a rack.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n5EIxiNYzpY
Uploaded 2024-03-21.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 380°F (190°C) 20 - 25 mins; Air fryer 340°F (170°C)  18 mins.

recipes.title: SWEET and Sour CHICKEN Egg Fried Rice Takeaway at Home
ingredients: Orange juice — juice of 1 orange (about 150–180 ml; from a carton in the video)
Dark soy sauce — a good ½ tbsp
Cornstarch slurry — 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 3 tbsp water
Chicken seasoning powder — 1 tsp (plus a little for the chicken)
Onion, peppers and carrots (amounts not stated)
steps: Poach the chicken: Put the chicken breasts in a pan of water, bring to the boil, boil about 12 minutes, then turn off and remove to cool.

Make the sauce base: In a pan, combine the water, sugar, vinegar, soy sauce, ketchup and orange juice and heat. Add red colouring if you like, then stir in the cornstarch slurry to a loose, semi-thick consistency. This base can be cooled and stored; thicken it further when you use it.
Make the batter: Mix the self-raising flour with chicken powder, white pepper, salt and sugar, then whisk in the water and egg until smooth.
Batter the chicken: Cube the cooked chicken like nuggets, toss with a little chicken powder, then coat in the batter.

Fry twice: Heat the oil in a pan, fry the chicken in batches until puffed and lightly golden, and remove. Return them all to the oil and fry again until crisp and brown. (Freeze after the first fry if you like.)

Make the fried rice: Heat a little oil, stir the garlic, crack in the eggs and let them set briefly, then push them around. Add the day-old rice and break up the clumps. Add MSG, sugar, white pepper, salt and soy sauce and cook until dry. Stir in green onions.
Stir fry the sweet and sour: In the same pan with a little oil, soften the onions and peppers, add the carrots and pineapple, then pour in the sweet and sour sauce and thicken with a little slurry.
Serve: Serve the chicken balls with the sweet and sour and the egg fried rice.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=15k4kOtM_qE
Uploaded 2024-03-20.

recipes.title: Corned BEEF HASH Suet Pudding
ingredients: Butter — 40 g (some for greasing the basin)
Medium potatoes, peeled and diced (about 1 cm) — 2
Salt and pepper — to taste (no salt in the video; corned beef is salty)
Gravy made from cubes/granules — ½ cup
steps: Fry the potatoes and onion: Heat the oil, add the onion and the raw diced potatoes, season with pepper, and stir fry until the potatoes are cooked.
Add the corned beef: Mash the corned beef a little and add it with a pinch of thyme and about 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce.
Thicken with gravy: Pour in the gravy and cook until thick and absorbed, letting it catch and caramelise a little if you can. Cool.
Make the crust: Mix the flour, suet, salt and thyme. Use a little of the butter to grease the pudding basin, then rub the rest in to breadcrumbs. Add about 2½ tbsp water and bring together.
Line the basin: Keep a piece back for the lid. Roll out the rest and press it into the basin, patching any tears, with a small lip over the top.
Fill and seal: Pack in the hash, wet the edge, add the rolled lid and fold the lip over to seal.
Cover: Top with greaseproof paper, then foil scrunched tightly around the rim to keep water out.
Steam: Stand the basin on a trivet in a large pan, pour boiling water to between halfway and three-quarters up the side, cover and steam about 1 hour–1 hour 10 minutes.
Serve: Remove the foil and paper, and turn out onto a plate.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jMgxxoJpeRE
Uploaded 2024-03-19.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Baked Beans Heinz-Style
ingredients: Navy beans or small white (haricot) beans, soaked overnight, drained and rinsed — 900 g
Water — for boiling the beans (about 1½ in above them)
Water/veg stock/chicken stock (the bean cooking water in the video) — 2 cups
Veg stock cube — 1 (used in the video)
Water — ¼ cup (60 ml), adjust as needed
Apple cider vinegar — ¼ cup (60 ml), adjust to your ketchup
Brown sugar — ¼ cup (50 g), adjust to your ketchup
Cornstarch — 2 tbsp dissolved in ¼ cup (60 ml) water
steps: Boil the beans: Put the soaked beans in a pan with water about 1½ in above them. Bring to the boil, skim off the scum, then simmer about 1–1½ hours, stirring now and then, skimming and keeping the water above the beans, until plump but still with some texture.
Drain: Drain the beans, keeping the cooking water.

Make the sauce: In a pan, combine the sugar, ketchup, tomato paste, vinegar, spices, salt and pepper. Add some of the bean water and crumble in a veg stock cube, then heat and stir to bring the flavours together.
Cook the beans in the sauce: Add the beans and simmer about 15–20 minutes.
Thicken: Stir in the cornstarch slurry (made with bean water in the video) to a good consistency, thinning with water if it goes too thick.
Store: Cool. Keep in the fridge up to 7 days or freeze in portions for up to 3 months; reheat slowly, adding a little water.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rSx18y6EqjY
Uploaded 2024-03-18.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Cook 1 ½ hours; Cook in sauce 15-20 mins.

recipes.title: Sausage Plait @HYSapientia
ingredients: Ready-rolled puff pastry — as much as you need
Dried sage — 2 tsp (fresh in the video)
Cayenne pepper — ¼ tsp (adjust to taste)
Small onion, finely grated or diced — 1
steps: Prep: Roughly mince the garlic, finely dice the onion, chop the sage, and cut the peeled apple into small chunks.

Mix: Combine the pork and beef with the garlic, onion, sage, apple, breadcrumbs, salt, pepper, thyme, smoked paprika, nutmeg, garlic powder, cayenne and Worcestershire sauce. Mix well by hand for a couple of minutes. (You can sauté the onion and garlic first if you prefer.)
Preheat: Heat the oven to 190°C (air fryer 180°C). Line a tray with baking parchment.
Shape: Roll the meat into a long sausage shape and lay it down the middle of the pastry.
Cut the plait: Cut a triangle at each end to fold up, then cut diagonal strips down both sides, with the same number on each side.
Plait: Fold up the end flaps, then bring the strips over the filling alternately from each side to make a lattice. Lift onto the tray.
Bake: Brush with egg wash and bake about 30–35 minutes in an oven (25–30 in the air fryer) until golden and the meat is cooked through.
Serve: Let it cool a little before slicing; serve with anything you like, such as baked beans.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Nm0-jfydPX0
Uploaded 2024-03-17.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 380°F (190°C) – 30 - 35  mins cook; Air fryer 360°F (180°C)  – 25 - 30 mins cook.

recipes.title: IRISH Coffee INSTANT
ingredients: Instant coffee of choice — 3 tbsp (at least a good couple)
Heavy or whipping cream — a little
Optional topping — grated nutmeg or chocolate
steps: Froth the cream: Whip the cream in a jug with a handheld frother until fairly thick but not stiff. Set aside.
Warm the glass: Pour some boiling water into an Irish coffee glass to warm it, then tip it out.
Make the coffee: Make strong instant coffee with the coffee and boiling water.
Sweeten: Put the brown sugar in the warmed glass and pour in a little coffee to dissolve it, then add more coffee.
Add whiskey: Pour in the whiskey and stir.
Float the cream: Pour the cream gently over the back of a spoon so it floats on top.
Serve: Grate over chocolate or nutmeg if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JamHP5DcvHg
Uploaded 2024-03-16.

recipes.title: BUTTER Pasty FRIDAY Pasty TRADITIONAL LANCASHIRE dish with a twist, Meatless Friday's Pi Day
ingredients: Potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced — 1 lb (450 g)
Unsalted butter — 4 tbsp, plus a little for the filling
Salt and pepper — to taste (no salt in the video; the cheddar is salty)
steps: Par-boil the potatoes: Slice the potatoes evenly, cover with water in a pan, bring to the boil and boil 6 minutes until they take a fork. Drain and cool a little.
Fry the onions: Melt a good amount of butter over gentle heat and fry the sliced onions with a good pinch of dried thyme and black pepper until soft (some caramelisation is fine). Turn off the heat.
Preheat: Heat the oven to 180°C (air fryer 175°C).
Fill: Lay the puff pastry bases on a tray. Layer potato and onion in the middle, then a little dab of mustard, cheddar and some mozzarella, and a little butter.
Seal: Bring the pastry over the top (lift the bottom up to meet it if overfilled) and squash the edges together.
Finish: Brush with milk and poke a couple of small vent holes.
Bake: Bake about 20 minutes until golden. Let them cool a little before cutting.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LMWLu6izQ7M

Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 360°F (180°C) – 20 mins cook; Air fryer 350°F (175°C)  – 20 mins cook.

recipes.title: Tart With Rasher IRISH Dish
ingredients: Beaten egg — for sealing the case
Irish bacon rashers (smoked streaky and loin end in the video), diced — 8 (10 smaller ones in the video)
Heavy cream — 1 cup (or milk or evaporated milk)
Grated cheese (cheddar, Gruyère or a mix) — 1 cup
Salt and freshly ground black pepper — to taste (only pepper in the video; the bacon is salty)
Fresh chives or parsley, chopped — for garnish
steps: Make the pastry: Rub the shortening and butter into the flour and salt, then mix in the egg beaten with the water and vinegar and bring together.

Line the dish: Preheat the oven to 190°C. Put a circle of parchment in the base of a deep dish, roll out the pastry and line the dish, trimming the edge. Prick the base with a fork. Keep the trimmings for another use.
Blind bake: Line with crumpled parchment and baking beads and bake 15 minutes.
Fry the bacon: Meanwhile, stir fry the diced bacon and onion in a dry pan in the bacon's own fat until cooked (browning is fine). Cool.
Seal the case: Remove the beads, brush the inside with beaten egg and bake 3–4 minutes more to seal.
Make the custard: Beat the eggs with the cream, black pepper and a little nutmeg.

Fill: Spread the bacon and onion in the case without packing it down, pour over the custard, and scatter about a cup of cheddar on top, tapping it so it sinks just under the surface. Add a little more cheese on top.
Bake: Bake about 20 minutes until set.
Serve: Cool about 10 minutes, turn out using a plate, and garnish with chives or parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C71l9cHG6Ug
Uploaded 2024-03-14.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 380°F (190°C)  15 mins – seal 4 mins – 20 mins cook; Air fryer 33600°F (180°C)  15 mins – seal 4 mins – 20 mins cook.

recipes.title: Portuguese egg custard tarts Pastéis de Nata @HYSapientia
ingredients: Cinnamon stick — 1 (or ¼ tsp ground cinnamon)
Orange peel, pith removed — 1 strip (about 2 in)
Puff pastry, thawed — 1 sheet (fresh works best, per the description)
steps: Make the syrup: Heat the water and sugar with the lemon peel and cinnamon until the sugar dissolves and it comes to the boil. Turn off and leave to infuse and cool.
Infuse the milk: In another pan, gently heat the milk with the orange peel, vanilla and cream until tiny bubbles appear (don't burn it). Set aside to cool (traditionally about 15 minutes).
Mix the yolks: Break up the egg yolks and mix well with the sugar and cornstarch.
Combine: Remove the orange peel, pour the milk into the yolks and mix, then add about ⅔ cup of the syrup. Let it settle.
Shape the pastry: Roll the pastry sheet up into a log, cut it into pieces, flatten each piece and press it into a tart cup so the top edge stays thick and the base is thin.
Fill: Preheat the oven as hot as it goes (about 215–230°C). Sieve the custard into a jug and fill the cups about three-quarters full.
Bake: Bake about 18–25 minutes (the description says 18 minutes in the air fryer; 24 was too long) until the custard rises and has dark brown spots.
Cool: Let them cool about 10 minutes before eating.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Il-ZFGtBz5s
Uploaded 2024-03-13.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 430°F (215°C)  20 -25 mins; Air fryer 430°F (215°C)  18 mins. I cooked at 24 mins, which was too long. After reducing the time, the second tray of tarts had better colour.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: OFFALY Bacon Loaf COUNTY Offaly IRELAND
ingredients: Bacon, minced or finely diced (smoked in the video) — 1 lb (450 g)
Oil or butter — for softening the onion
Breadcrumbs — 1 cup (about 1½ cups in the video)
Milk — ½ cup (about 1 cup in the video)
Fresh parsley, finely chopped — ¼ cup
Fresh thyme leaves — 1 tsp (or ½ tsp dried)
steps: Soak the breadcrumbs: Pour the milk over the breadcrumbs and let them soak.
Dice the bacon: Finely dice (or mince) the bacon. Preheat the oven to 175°C (air fryer 170°C).
Soften the aromatics: Gently soften the onion and garlic in a little oil or butter, then add them to the breadcrumb mixture.
Mix: Add the pork mince, bacon, thyme, parsley, pepper, salt, nutmeg, whiskey and beaten eggs, and mix without overworking.
Make the glaze: Mix the brown sugar, ketchup, mustard powder and vinegar.
Fill the tin: Line a loaf tin with parchment (or butter it well) and press the mixture in loosely without compacting. Spread some glaze on top, keeping the rest back.
Bake covered: Cover with foil, set on a tray and bake 1 hour.
Glaze and finish: Remove the foil, spread over the remaining glaze, and bake about 20–24 minutes more until sticky and caramelised.
Serve: Rest briefly, then slice.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-JWfBsNFOV8
Uploaded 2024-03-11.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 350°F (175°C)   1 hr foil on. Add glaze 24 mins cook; Air fryer 340°F (170°C)    1 hr foil on. Add glaze 24 mins cook.

recipes.title: Macaroni Pie SCOTTISH Comfort Staple
ingredients: Sharp cheddar, grated — 2 cups (or as much as you like), plus extra for the top
steps: Cook the macaroni: Boil the macaroni as per the packet until just al dente. Drain, toss with a splash of olive oil, and cool.
Make the pastry: Rub the fats into the flour and salt, then bring together with the egg beaten with the water and vinegar.
Line the tins: Roll out the pastry and press it into 5 in tins (base lined with paper), leaving an overhang, then trim. Prick the bases.
Blind bake: Preheat to 180–190°C. Line with crumpled parchment and baking beads and bake about 15 minutes.
Make the custard: Beat the eggs with the milk, mustard powder, black pepper, salt and nutmeg, then stir in the cheddar (and mozzarella). Mix in the cooled macaroni.
Seal: Remove the beads, brush the bases with beaten egg and bake a couple of minutes (about 4) to seal.
Fill and top: Divide the macaroni mixture between the cases and top with a little more cheddar and Parmesan (breadcrumbs optional).
Bake: Bake about 20–24 minutes until set and golden.
Serve: Cool about 10 minutes before removing from the tins and cutting.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IzrFjK4tGBw
Uploaded 2024-03-10.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 380°F (190°C)  15 mins – seal 4 mins – 24 mins cook; Air fryer 33600°F (180°C)  15 mins – seal 4 mins – 24 mins cook.

recipes.title: SAVOURY Pepperoni BREAD PUDDING Pizza Style
ingredients: Marinara/pizza sauce — 1½ cups, plus more for serving
Heavy cream — ½ cup (optional, for a richer custard)
Fresh basil, chopped — 1 tbsp, plus extra to garnish
Smoked paprika — just over ½ tsp (from the video)
Red pepper, onion and garlic, finely diced (from the video)
Chopped ham (optional, used in the video)
Salt and black pepper — to taste
steps: Make the custard: Beat the eggs, then whisk in the evaporated milk, oregano, black pepper, smoked paprika and the chopped basil. Set aside.

Sauté the veg: Dice the pepper and red onion small and crush the garlic. Fry briefly in a little olive oil just to bring out the flavour, then let it cool so it doesn't cook the eggs. Stir in the chopped ham and some chopped pepperoni. The pepperoni and sauce are salty, so go easy on salt.
Soak the bread: Trim only the very driest crusts, tear the bread into the custard, stir, and let it soak up the milk. Stir in the cooled veg mixture.
Layer: Grease the dish with butter. Spread half the bread mixture loosely in the dish, then add a layer of marinara sauce, a layer of pepperoni and a layer of grated mozzarella.
Top: Spoon the rest of the bread mixture loosely over, press down gently without squashing, then dot with more pepperoni and mozzarella, grated Parmesan and black pepper.

Bake: Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C (360°F) or air fryer at 170°C (340°F) for about 15 minutes per the description (the video bakes about 24–25 minutes) until the cheese top is crusty. Cut through the top while it's warm and serve with extra marinara.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2O4sY3Bex-U
Uploaded 2024-03-09.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 360°F (180°C)  15 mins; Air fryer 340°F (170°C)  15 mins.

recipes.title: IRISH MASH POTATO Pastry  APPLE cake. More a pie than a cake really. . .
ingredients: Plain flour, plus more as needed
Mixed apples (cooking and eating), peeled, cored and sliced or chunked, with about 3 eating apples cut into chunks and kept separate
Lemon juice — to stop browning, plus juice of ½ lemon for the pan
English mixed spice — about 1 tsp (or up to 1 tsp cinnamon and about ¼ tsp nutmeg)
Brown sugar — about 1½ heaped tbsp, to taste
Cornflour/cornstarch — 1 tbsp, mixed with about 1 tbsp water
steps: Make the potato pastry: Mix the butter, flour, mashed potato and salt by hand into a workable dough. If the potato is wet, add more flour until it is no longer sticky (no water needed). Leave it in the bowl.

Prep the apples: Peel and slice the apples, some thin to break down and some in chunks. Keep about three eating apples, cut in chunks, in a separate bowl. Squeeze lemon over both bowls to stop them browning.

Cook the filling: Melt butter in a pan, add the main apples with salt and the juice of half a lemon, and cook until juice forms. Add the spice, then the brown sugar, and cook, stirring, until much of the apple is soft and mushy. Taste and adjust the sugar.
Add texture and thicken: Stir in the reserved eating-apple chunks, then the cornflour slurry. It thickens at once. Turn off the heat and let it cool.
Line the tin: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Line a 7-inch springform tin and press the soft potato pastry into it, leaving an overhang and patching any tears.
Fill and top: Spoon in the cooled filling. Press the remaining pastry out on a floured surface into a lid, lay it over, fold in from the sides, and neaten the edge.
Glaze and vent: Brush egg wash on the top only, not down the sides, and cut a vent for steam.
Bake: Put the tin on a tray and bake for about 20–22 minutes, checking from about 17 minutes, until golden.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pgKNcTomTgE
Uploaded 2024-03-08.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 375°F (190°C).  Bake 25 mins; Air fryer 360°F (180°C).  Bake 22 mins.

recipes.title: Pickled COCKLES Traditional BRITISH SEAFOOD Snack
ingredients: Boiled baby clams or cockle meat (shelled)
Salt — for rinsing, plus a little for the brine
Water — about the same amount as the vinegar
steps: Rinse the cockles: Tip the cockle meat into a bowl, add some salt and water, swish to rinse out any sand, then drain.
Make the brine: In a pan, mix apple cider vinegar with roughly the same amount of water, then add sugar, a little salt, the peppercorns, coriander seed, bay leaves and chilli if using.
Infuse: Bring to the boil, stirring to dissolve the sugar, boil for a couple of minutes, then turn off and let it cool. Strain out the spices if you like.
Jar: Pack the drained cockles into sterilised jars, pour in the brine to cover, and put the lids on. The video then cans the jars so they seal.
Wait: Leave the jars at least a week before eating so the cockles take on the vinegar; longer is better.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lTS2hbja3nU
Uploaded 2024-03-07.

recipes.title: Kentish CHEESE Casserole BRITISH cuisine
ingredients: Onions (red, white or mixed), thinly sliced
Butter — a lump, plus a little for the top
Salt and black pepper — to taste
Brown (or white) sugar — about ½ tbsp
steps: Soften the onions: Put the chopped garlic, a lump of butter and a little olive oil in a pan, add the thinly sliced onions, season with salt and pepper, and sauté until soft. A little colour is fine.

Simmer in stock: Add just over a cup of veg stock and boil, uncovered, so some of the liquid cooks off. Stir in about half a tablespoon of brown sugar. Cook no more than about 5 minutes so it stays saucy, then turn off the heat.
Preheat: Heat the oven to 190°C (380°F), or an air fryer oven to about 170°C (340°F).
Layer: In a baking dish, alternate layers of the onion mixture and grated cheddar, using as much cheese as you like.
Top: Cover with a layer of breadcrumbs and press down lightly, then dot with butter and sprinkle with a little more cheese and pepper.
Bake: Bake for about 25 minutes until bubbling with a crunchy top. Let it cool for about 10 minutes before serving.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yBYD3VrJhag
Uploaded 2024-03-06.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 380°F (190°C) 20 - 25 mins; Air fryer 360°F (180°C)  20-25  mins.

recipes.title: BUTTER Pie FRIDAY Pie TRADITIONAL LANCASHIRE dish @HYSapientia
ingredients: Shortcrust pastry (homemade or shop-bought ready-rolled), for a base and lid
Potatoes, sliced to an even thickness (a couple for a small pie; 1.5–2 kg for a big one)
Butter — for frying, plus knobs for the layers
Salt — to taste (careful if using salted butter)
steps: Slice: Slice the onions, and slice the potatoes to the same thickness so they cook evenly.

Par-boil the potatoes: Cover the potatoes with cold water, bring to the boil, and boil for 5 minutes only, stirring once so they cook evenly, until a knife just goes in but they still have a bite. Drain.
Soften the onions: Fry the onions in butter over a medium-low flame with a little black pepper until soft (browning isn't the aim). Turn off and let cool.

Line the tin: Preheat the oven to about 190–200°C (380–400°F); the air fryer oven in the video uses 180°C. Roll out the pastry and line a pie tin about 8 inches across and 1 inch deep, leaving an overhang. Roll out a lid.
Layer: Layer potato slices and onions, adding knobs of butter, pepper and salt to taste between layers, until full.
Seal: Brush the rim with egg wash, lay on the lid, then fold the overhanging pastry over to seal bottom to top into a thick crust. Crimp with your fingers.
Vent and glaze: Cut air vents in the top and brush with egg wash.
Bake: Bake on a tray for up to 25 minutes until golden. Rest for about 5 minutes, then slice, or turn out onto a plate to serve.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PT7OU6YhjiI
Uploaded 2024-03-05.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 380°F (190°C) 20 - 25 mins; Air fryer 360°F (180°C)  20-25  mins.

recipes.title: YORKSHIRE Curd Tart TRADITIONAL Dessert
ingredients: Milk — the video uses a large reduced carton (5 L of milk in total)
Apple cider vinegar — 2–3 tbsp (or white vinegar or lemon juice)
Plain flour and fats (butter/lard), the usual shortcrust mix
Eggs, beaten (a little kept back to seal the case)
Fruit — a handful (the video doesn't name it)
steps: Curdle the milk: Heat the milk in a pan, stirring so it doesn't catch, until it boils. Add 2–3 tbsp apple cider vinegar, stir, and keep it on a low heat for about 10 more seconds as curds form, then turn off. Leave a couple of minutes.
Strain: Line a sieve over a bowl with a damp cotton cloth and ladle in the curds to drain. Don't press them, so they stay crumbly. Keep the whey for baking or the garden.
Make the pastry: Rub the fats into the flour and salt with light hands, mix in 1 tbsp sugar, then bring together with water.

Line and blind bake: Preheat the oven to 170–180°C (340–350°F), or up to 200°C. Roll out the pastry and line a 9-inch loose-bottom tin, leaving the excess on. Prick the base, line with parchment and fill with baking beads or rice. Blind bake for 15 minutes.
Seal the case: Remove the beads, brush the inside with beaten egg, and bake for another 3–5 minutes. Trim off the excess pastry.
Mix the filling: Beat the remaining egg into the curds with a couple of tablespoons of sugar, about ¼ cup cream if using, and the lemon zest, keeping some curd texture. Stir in some fruit.
Fill: Spoon the filling into the case, push it to the edges, dot with a little more fruit, and add a pinch of nutmeg.
Bake: Bake for about 15 minutes until set and lightly firm. Cool for at least 10 minutes, ideally until cool, before slicing.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IokI8H6ullY
Uploaded 2024-03-04.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven cook 180 / 360 15 mins; air fryer 175 / 350 15 mins.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: CHIVITO ICONIC National dish of URUGUAY
ingredients: Thinly sliced beef (frozen first so it slices thin) or a thicker steak
steps: Toast the bread: Spread mayo on the cut sides of the bread, let it soak in, then toast mayo side down in a pan over a moderate flame until lightly browned. Give the other side a quick toast too.
Char the peppers: Dry-fry the red pepper slices for a quick smoky char, then add a splash of olive oil, sear briefly, and remove.
Cook the bacon: Fry the streaky bacon to how crisp you like it, then remove.

Sear the beef: Cook the thin beef slices in the bacon fat for just a minute, turning once. Overlap them in the pan to fit the bread, top with mozzarella, cover with a lid until melted, then turn off the heat.

Build: On the bottom half, spread mayo, then add lettuce, tomato, the cheesy beef, plenty of bacon, ham, the soft-boiled egg, the peppers, sliced green olives and more mayo. Put the top on and cut diagonally.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tX3fN9AG_ik
Uploaded 2024-03-03.

recipes.title: IRISH Potato Bread Farls / Tattie Griddle Scones Recipe
ingredients: Potatoes (old ones are fine), peeled and cut up
Butter — a decent lump for the mash, plus more for frying
Salt — to taste (less if using salted butter)
Plain flour — enough to form a soft dough, plus more for dusting
steps: Boil the potatoes: Cover the potato pieces with water (unsalted), bring to the boil, lid on if you like, and cook until a fork goes in easily. Drain.
Dry them: Return the potatoes to the pan over the flame and shake until the sizzling stops and they're dry and fluffy.
Mash: Mash (or rice) the potatoes, then mix in a decent lump of butter and salt to taste.
Add flour while warm: Tip in the flour and stir until fully incorporated. Do this while the potatoes are still warm, or it won't come together.

Shape: Turn onto a floured surface, flatten to cool slightly, then press or roll to about half an inch thick, using as much flour as needed. Cut into rounds with a large cutter or into triangles or wedges (six from a pan-sized round).

Cook: Melt a little butter in a pan over a low-medium heat and cook the farls for 2–3 minutes per side, flipping as often as you like, until golden. They can also be dry-fried for a lighter crust. Add more butter for each batch.
Serve or freeze: Serve hot with butter and a fried egg, or cool and freeze for later.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6abrzl4pqR8
Uploaded 2024-03-02.

recipes.title: Colcannon FULL IRISH Not Traditional
ingredients: Potatoes, peeled and diced for mash
Spring onions (green onions), trimmed and cut into fairly large pieces
Butter — plenty (for the milk, cabbage, mash and ham)
Vinegar — a splash, for the egg water
steps: Boil the potatoes and cabbage: Boil the diced potatoes in salted water. In another pan, boil the sliced cabbage for 5–6 minutes, then drain.
Infuse the milk: Warm a little milk with plenty of butter, add the spring onions, and cook gently until soft so the milk takes on the onion flavour. Set aside.
Butter the cabbage: Toss the drained cabbage in a pan with a little butter and pepper for a minute (don't brown it).
Make the colcannon: Drain the fork-tender potatoes, dry them back on the heat, and mash with some texture left in. Mash in butter, then stir in the cabbage and the onion-milk mixture.
Fry the ham: Fry the smoked ham pieces in a little butter until lightly coloured. Keep the pan fat.

Soft-boil the eggs: Bring water with a splash of vinegar to the boil, gently lower in the room-temperature eggs, cover, and cook on a medium flame for 5 minutes. Move them to cold water, cool, then peel gently.

Assemble: Preheat the oven to about 180°C (350°F). Spread colcannon in a dish, press the ham into it, make wells, and set the eggs in. Gently cover them with more colcannon, season with pepper (no salt, as the ham is salty), and drizzle with the ham and butter fat.
Bake: Bake until browned on top: the video estimates 12 minutes and takes it out at 20. Rest a minute before serving.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n6XtpbbW41M
Uploaded 2024-03-01.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Boil eggs 5 mins little vinegar in water. Take out into cold water. Peel; Oven 190 (380) - 200 (400) 12 mins crisp up the top.
