recipes.title: SCOTTISH Cranachan Traditional Dessert
ingredients: Whisky — a little for soaking oats, plus about 2 tbsp for the cream
Raspberries — plenty, some kept whole for topping
Honey — a little for the purée, a little for the cream, and an optional drizzle
steps: Toast the oats: Toast the oats in a dry pan over a gentle heat, keeping them moving so they don't catch, until lightly toasted. Let them cool.
Soak some oats: Put a small portion of the toasted oats in a bowl and douse lightly with whisky.
Make the purée: Blend some of the raspberries with a little sugar (optional) and a little honey.
Make the cream: Whip the cream with the cream cheese, then blend or fold in about 2 tbsp whisky and a little honey.
Ripple: Take out some of the cream and gently swirl a little purée through it for a ripple effect.
Layer: In glasses, layer whisky oats, raspberry purée, toasted oats and ripple cream, repeating as you like.
Top: Finish with the whisky-honey cream, fresh raspberries, a few whisky oats, and a very light drizzle of honey (optional).
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cejWniTh2pQ
Uploaded 2024-02-29.

recipes.title: SAVOURY MEDITERRANEAN Vegetable and Feta BREAD PUDDING
ingredients: Evaporated milk — 1 can, with a little kept back to rehydrate the garlic powder
Spanish hot smoked paprika — about ½ tsp
Sun-dried tomatoes in oil, with some of their roasted garlic and oil
Salt (a tiny amount) and black pepper
Optional extra cheese for the top (mozzarella or cheddar)
steps: Rehydrate the garlic: Stir garlic powder into a little evaporated milk and let it sit.

Sauté the veg: Put the diced courgette, onion and peppers in a pan with olive oil (the oil from the sun-dried tomato jar works well), a tiny pinch of salt and some black pepper. Stir-fry for about 5 minutes to release the juices, then stir in some sun-dried tomatoes and roasted garlic. Turn off the heat and let cool, keeping the juices.
Make the custard: Beat the 4 eggs with the rest of the evaporated milk, the garlic milk, about 1 tsp oregano and about ½ tsp smoked paprika.

Combine: Preheat the oven to 180°C (360°F). Tear the bread into the custard, add the basil and the cooled veg with their juices, and stir well. Stir in most of the olives, some Parmesan and some crumbled feta, then chunks of feta.
Fill the dish: Oil a baking dish and add the mixture loosely without squashing, tucking in more feta as you go. Top with feta, grated Parmesan, a drizzle of olive oil, olives and any extra cheese.
Bake: Bake for about 15 minutes at 180°C until the top is crispy.

Finish: Drizzle with a little olive oil, mark into six portions right away so the crisp top doesn't tear, loosen the edges, and scatter with the reserved olives and fresh parsley. Serve warm, or cold with a crisp salad.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tAERoD-xTDg
Uploaded 2024-02-28.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 380°F (180°C)  20 mins; Air fryer 340°F (180°C)  20 mins.

recipes.title: Traditional STAFFORDSHIRE OATCAKES 18th century
ingredients: Oatmeal (quick oats ground fine in a grinder)
Butter — for the pan and for spreading
steps: Mix the dry ingredients: Stir the flour, ground oatmeal, salt, sugar and instant yeast together. The yeast can be started in the milk and water first if you prefer.
Make the batter: Make a well, add the milk and water, and mix into a lump-free batter.
Rest: Cover and leave for an hour so the yeast works and bubbles form. Stir again in case the oats have sunk.

Cook: Heat a little butter in a pan over a medium-low heat, pour in a ladle of batter and swirl to spread. Cook until bubbles appear all over, flip, and cook a couple of minutes more, flipping as often as you like until coloured on both sides. Wipe a little fat around the pan between oatcakes.
Fill: Spread with butter or scatter with grated cheese, roll up, and serve hot.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=inUQ2OPa2ro
Uploaded 2024-02-27.

recipes.title: Corned BEEF and Onion Quiche DELICIOUS and HEARTY dish perfect for any meal
ingredients: Shortcrust pastry (butter and lard/shortening), or ready-rolled
Small onions — 2, mostly finely diced with a couple of rings kept for the top
Eggs — 4, beaten (a little used for the egg wash)
Salt and black pepper — to taste
Corned beef — 1 tin, broken into chunks
Worcestershire sauce — a dash (optional; mustard also works)
steps: Line the tin: Preheat the oven to 180–190°C (350–375°F). Roll out the pastry and line a 9-inch loose-base tin, leaving a lip over the edge. Prick the base all over.
Blind bake: Line with scrunched parchment and baking beads or rice, pushed out to the sides, and bake for 15 minutes.
Cook the onions: Fry the diced onion in butter with a small pinch of dried thyme until soft; a little colour is fine. Set aside.
Seal the case: Remove the beads, brush the base with some of the beaten egg, and bake for 3–5 minutes more to prevent a soggy bottom. Trim the overhanging crust.
Make the custard: Whisk the remaining eggs with a little cream, black pepper and a pinch of salt.

Fill: Spread the onions over the base, add the corned beef chunks and a dash of Worcestershire sauce, then a little cheese. Pour over the egg mixture and top with more cheese, pepper and the onion rings.
Bake: Bake for 20 minutes until set. Cool for about 10 minutes, remove from the tin, and sprinkle with fresh parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cZp-v6SVHZc
Uploaded 2024-02-26.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 380°F (190°C)  15 mins – seal 4 mins – 20 mins cook; Air fryer 33600°F (180°C)  15 mins – seal 4 mins – 20 mins cook.

recipes.title: FORFAR Bridies TRADITIONAL SCOTTISH meat pastry
ingredients: Plain flour and fats (the usual shortcrust mix)
Egg and water, with a little apple cider vinegar
Onion, grated and squeezed to remove excess moisture
Salt and black pepper — to taste
Beef stock cube — just over ¼, crumbled (optional)
steps: Make the pastry: Rub the fats into the flour, then mix in the beaten egg, water and apple cider vinegar and bring together by hand.

Mix the filling: Combine the minced beef and squeezed grated onion with salt, pepper, about 1 tsp mustard powder and a little crumbled stock cube, mixing by hand. Mix in the suet. The filling goes in raw and dry.
Preheat: Heat the oven to 190–200°C (380–400°F); the air fryer oven in the video uses 170°C.
Portion: Divide the filling into five portions and the pastry into five pieces.
Shape: Roll out each piece of pastry, add the filling to one half, wet the edge with water, fold into a half-moon, and seal and crimp.
Vent and glaze: Make a steam hole in the top of each bridie and brush with egg wash.
Bake: Bake for about 35 minutes until golden, cooking the filling through from raw. Let them cool a little before eating.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kOi57St2yLw

Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 400°F (200°C)  35 mins; Air fryer 340°F (170°C)  35 mins.

recipes.title: SAVOURY Spinach and Cheese,  BREAD PUDDING
ingredients: Day-old bread, crusts thinly trimmed (save them for breadcrumbs)
Evaporated milk — 1 tin (or milk or cream)
Garlic powder — a little, rehydrated in some of the evaporated milk
Spinach — a couple of cups or more, roughly chopped, stalks finely chopped (or defrosted, squeezed frozen spinach)
Butter (or oil) — for frying and greasing
Salt and black pepper — to taste
Grated cheese — a good handful, plus more for the top
Bacon bits, pre-fried — about a good cupful, plus more (or ham or Spam, or leave out)
steps: Rehydrate the garlic: Stir the garlic powder into a little evaporated milk and leave it to absorb.

Cook the veg: Gently sauté the garlic and onion in butter with pepper and salt until translucent. Add the chopped spinach stalks for a minute, then the leaves, and cook until wilted. Let it cool so it won't cook the eggs.
Make the custard: Beat the eggs with mustard powder and seasoning, then add the garlic milk and the rest of the evaporated milk. Stir in a good handful of cheese and a cupful of bacon bits.
Add the bread: Break the bread into chunks, stir into the custard to soak up as much as possible, then add more bacon and the cooled spinach and onion.

Bake: Preheat the oven to 180°C (360°F). Butter a dish, spoon the mixture in without smoothing it, and top with grated cheese. Bake for up to 20 minutes until crispy and brown on top (the video's air fryer oven was done in about 13).
Serve: Cut through the cheesy top into portions (about six) while hot, run a knife around the edge, and serve.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AfWijF7lXbY
Uploaded 2024-02-24.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 380°F (180°C)  20 mins; Air fryer 340°F (180°C)  20 mins NOTE: 12 -13 mins and mine was cooked.

recipes.title: 1940's WAR TIME RECIPE WOOLTON Pie Both pastry
ingredients: Cold water — only if the mix is dry
Celery, parsnip, carrot, turnip and potato, peeled and chopped
Mushrooms, wiped and sliced or chunked
Dried thyme — a good pinch (or fresh herbs)
Cornflour — less than ½ tbsp, mixed with water
steps: Make the potato pastry: At room temperature, rub the butter into the flour and salt, then work in the mashed potato and bring together. Add water only if it's dry.

Make the oat pastry: Rub the butter and shortening into the flour, oatmeal and salt, then add a little water and bring together without overworking. It will be firm and crumbly. Cover both pastries and rest on the side.
Sauté: Melt butter in a pan and sauté the leek and onion with a pinch of salt, pepper and dried thyme without browning.

Simmer: Add the potatoes, the other root veg and the mushrooms, then 300 ml veg stock. Cover and cook for about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Uncover to cook off some of the liquid once the potatoes just take a fork.
Thicken: Stir in the cornflour slurry to coat the veg, turn off the heat, and let the filling cool.

Top: Pour the cooled filling into a pie dish. Roll the soft potato pastry thickly on a floured surface and carefully lay it over one half. Roll the oat pastry, neaten its edge, and cover the other half so the two meet. Tuck the pastry in and leave it over the sides.
Bake: Preheat the oven to about 180°C (350°F). Cut vent holes (no egg wash, as in wartime) and bake for about 20 minutes. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GvGAPJnUzF0
Uploaded 2024-02-23.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 380°F (180°C)  20 mins; Air fryer 340°F (180°C)  20 mins.

recipes.title: Colcannon TRADITIONAL IRISH dish
ingredients: Potatoes, peeled and diced for mash
Spring onions (green onions), trimmed and cut into fairly large pieces
Butter — plenty (for the milk, cabbage, mash and to serve)
steps: Boil the potatoes: Boil the diced potatoes in salted water until fork tender.
Boil the cabbage: Meanwhile, boil the sliced cabbage for 5–6 minutes at most, then drain.
Infuse the milk: Warm a little milk with a generous amount of butter, add the spring onions, and cook gently until softened so the milk takes on the onion flavour. Turn off the heat.
Butter the cabbage: Toss the drained cabbage in a pan with a little butter and pepper just to coat (don't brown it).
Mash: Drain the potatoes, dry them back on the heat, then mash, leaving some texture. Mash in plenty of butter.
Combine: Stir in the cabbage and the onion-milk mixture until evenly mixed.
Serve: Pile onto a dish, make a well in the centre, and fill it with more butter.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EB-D4S34uyU
Uploaded 2024-02-22.

recipes.title: CREMPOG Traditional WELSH 200 years BEFORE AMERICAN Pancakes
ingredients: Milk — 1 cup per cup of buttermilk needed
Apple cider (or other) vinegar — 1 tbsp per cup of milk
Milk — a little, for the yeast
Sugar — about 1 tbsp for the yeast, plus a little for the batter
Plain flour (a little more than the modern version)
steps: Start the yeast: Mix a little milk with about 1 tsp yeast and about 1 tbsp sugar and leave for 5–10 minutes to activate.
Make buttermilk: Stir 1 tbsp vinegar into each cup of milk and leave it to curdle. Make one portion for each batter.

Traditional batter: Mix the flour with a little sugar and a pinch of salt, then beat in an egg, the yeasted milk, some milk and the buttermilk until lump-free. Cover and rest for 45 minutes to an hour until bubbly.
Modern batter: Mix the flour with salt, baking powder and baking soda, then beat in an egg, the buttermilk and some melted butter. Rest for about 30 minutes.

Cook: Heat a pan with a little butter over a moderate heat (not too hot). Ladle in batter, cook until bubbles appear, flip, and cook the other side. Add butter between pancakes. For blueberry ones, use a little less batter and drop blueberries on top before flipping.
Serve: Serve the heavier traditional crempog with bacon, cabbage or leeks, and the lighter modern ones like everyday pancakes.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R7VDh5zxCaA

recipes.title: Baked Apple and Pear Charlotte TRADITIONAL British dessert  @HYSapientia
ingredients: Eating apples and pears (any kind), peeled, cored and sliced
Lemon — juice of ½, squeezed into the soaking water
Day-old bread, crusts removed, thickly sliced (sliced bread works too)
Butter (or margarine) — for the bread, the fruit and the tin
Sugar — about 1 tbsp (to taste), plus a little for the top
Marmalade (or apricot or blackberry jam) — a spoonful (optional)
Cornflour — about 1 tbsp, mixed with about 1 tbsp water
steps: Prep the fruit: Squeeze half a lemon into a bowl of water. Peel, core and slice the apples and pears, cutting out any bruises, and keep them submerged in the lemon water.
Butter the bread: Cut the crusts off the bread, slice it fairly thick, and butter one side of each slice.

Cook the fruit: Tip the fruit and its lemony water into a pan and cook down without letting it go to mush. Taste and add about 1 tbsp sugar, a pinch of salt, mixed spice, a couple of knobs of butter, more lemon juice if you like, and a spoonful of marmalade.
Thicken: Stir in the cornflour slurry and cook, stirring, until glossy and thick but with texture left. Let it cool a little.

Line the tin: Butter an 8-inch springform tin (a 7-inch tin suits less fruit). Press buttered bread, butter side to the tin, over the base, then overlap slices up the sides, squashing them onto the base to seal.
Fill and top: Set the tin on a tray, spoon in the fruit, then cover with more buttered bread (cut and overlap to fit), fold the sides over, and press down. Sprinkle with a little sugar.

Bake: Bake at 180°C (350°F). Once the top is nicely brown, cover with foil for about 14 minutes so the sides and base cook through, then uncover for about 3 minutes to finish browning without blackening.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m_4ax6wl2Wc
Uploaded 2024-02-20.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 380°F (190°C)  15 mins; Air fryer 360°F (180°C)  15 mins.

recipes.title: Corned Beef Cottage Pie SIMPLE WEEKNIGHT Meal
ingredients: Potatoes, peeled and diced small for mash
Butter — for the mash and the onions
Grated cheese — some for the mash, more for the top
Gravy made from granules — 500 ml (use the potato water)
Corned beef — 1 tin (2 for a bigger family portion)
steps: Boil the potatoes: Boil the diced potatoes (salt the water if you like) until tender. Drain, keeping the potato water for the gravy.
Make the cheesy mash: Dry the potatoes back on the heat, add butter and pepper, and mash, leaving some texture. Stir in a little grated cheese and set aside.

Make the gravy base: Preheat the oven to 170–180°C (340–350°F). Fry the onion in butter with pepper and a good pinch of thyme, then stir in 1 tbsp tomato purée and about 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce. Add 500 ml gravy made with the potato water, then the frozen veg, and cook to your preferred thickness.
Layer: Spoon the veg and most of the gravy into a baking dish (keep a little gravy back for serving). Break the corned beef into chunks and spread it evenly over the top.
Top: Spread the cheesy mash over, leaving it rough so it crusts, then add the remaining cheese and some pepper.

Bake: Bake for about 15–20 minutes until the top is browned and crisp (everything inside is already cooked). Mark into portions before the cheese sets, rest a couple of minutes, and serve with the reserved gravy.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bCERuvePKjY
Uploaded 2024-02-19.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: oven to 380°F (180°C)  15-20 mins; Air fryer 340°F (170°C)  15-20 mins.

recipes.title: CLAPSHOT  Traditional SCOTTISH dish ORKNEY Islands
ingredients: Swede (the yellow/orange-fleshed root), peeled and cubed
Butter — plenty, plus more to serve
Salt and black pepper — to taste
steps: Prep: Chop the chives and set aside. Peel and chop the potatoes small, and peel and cube the swede.
Boil: Put the potatoes and swede in one pan of water and boil until very tender.
Dry: Drain, return the pan to a low flame, and stir until the excess moisture has steamed off and the mix is fluffy.
Mash: Turn off the heat and mash, leaving some texture if you like.
Season: Stir in plenty of butter, salt and black pepper, plus a little cream and a pinch of nutmeg if using, and most of the chives.
Serve: Pile into a dish, swirl the top with a fork, make a well in the middle, and add more butter and the remaining chives.

recipes.title: Eccles Cakes TRADITIONAL ENGLISH pastry ECCLES @HYSapientia
ingredients: Ready-made puff pastry, cut into squares
Mixed spice — ¾ tsp (or ½ tsp cinnamon and ¼ tsp nutmeg)
steps: Make the filling: Mix the currants, orange peel, brown sugar and ¾ tsp mixed spice, then stir in about 1 tbsp water to make a sticky mix.
Preheat: Heat the oven (an air fryer oven in the video) to 180°C (350°F).
Wrap: Put a spoonful of filling on each pastry square, bring the corners up into a parcel, twist to seal, and turn it over so the seam is underneath.
Flatten: Dust lightly with flour and roll each cake gently to flatten. Place on a lined tray.
Slit and glaze: Cut a couple of slits in the top of each, brush with egg white, and sprinkle with sugar.
Bake: Bake for about 15 minutes until golden and crisp underneath. Cool on a rack.

recipes.title: ANGLESEY Eggs TRADITIONAL Wyau Ynys Môn Welsh dish
ingredients: Butter — a good amount for the leeks, plus some for the mash, sauce and dishes
Potatoes, peeled and cut for boiling (some to mash, some to slice)
Milk — a little for the mash, plus more for the sauce
Grated cheese — for the sauce and the top
Eggs — 4 per dish (8 for both versions)
Mustard powder or mustard (optional, for the sauce)
steps: Cook the leeks: Melt a good amount of butter in a pan, add the sliced leeks with a little salt, and sweat them down gently without much browning, adding more butter and some black pepper. Let them cool.
Boil the potatoes: Boil the potatoes in salted water. Take some out while still firm for slicing (traditional) and cook the rest until soft for mash (modern).
Make the leek mash: Mash the soft potatoes with a little butter and milk, keeping some texture, and stir in some of the leeks.

Make the cheese sauce: Warm milk with a little cornflour, stirring so it doesn't catch, until it thickens like custard, then turn off the heat. Stir in a knob of butter and a handful of cheese, keeping some cheese back for the top.
Soft-boil the eggs: Boil the eggs for 5 minutes only, cool them immediately under the cold tap, and peel carefully.
Prep: Slice the firmer potatoes. Preheat the oven to about 170°C (340°F) and butter the baking dishes.

Modern version: Spread leek mash in a dish, make hollows for the eggs, leaving a channel round the edge, then set the eggs in. Cover gently with a little more mash, pour the cheese sauce over and down the sides, and top with cheese and pepper.
Traditional version: Layer the potato slices and leeks in a dish, make wells, set the eggs in, cover with a little potato, and top with cheese sauce, cheese and black pepper.
Bake: Bake each for about 20 minutes until bubbling and browned (everything inside is already cooked). Cut through the cheese before it sets and serve.

recipes.title: THE most RIDICULOUS Black Forest Cake 1970's revisited!
ingredients: Non-alcoholic cherry brandy (or kirsch or cherry brandy):
Fresh cherry juice (from juiced cherries) — ¼ cup
Fresh cherries, halved and stoned, plus a few whole for the top
steps: Make the batter: Mix the flour, baking soda, baking powder, sugar, cocoa and salt. Beat in the milk, eggs, oil, vanilla and water to a smooth chocolate batter.

Bake the layers: Preheat the oven to 175°C (350°F). Divide the batter evenly between three lined 7½-inch tins (the video weighs out about 443 g each) and bake for about 30–35 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Flatten: While each cake is hot, press another tin on top to flatten the dome. Turn out, peel off the lining, and cool, covered so they don't dry out.
Make the cherry syrup: Stir ¼ cup cherry juice with ½ tsp almond extract and about 1 tsp sugar until dissolved. Brush generously over each sponge.
Prep the fillings: Halve and stone the cherries, keeping some whole for the top. Grate the chocolate. Whip the cream with a little powdered sugar just until it holds (don't overwhip).
Layer: Spread cream on the first sponge, cover with halved cherries, and add a little more cream. Repeat with the second layer, then add the top sponge.
Finish: Spread cream over the top and around the sides, press grated chocolate onto the sides and top, and decorate with whole cherries.

recipes.title: CORNISH Raw Fry TRADITIONAL Cornwall ENGLAND
ingredients: Swede (rutabaga), peeled and sliced the same way
Smoked bacon, cubed (or lardons, ham or Spam)
Butter, lard or oil — a little
Salt (a little, as the bacon is salty) and black pepper
Veg stock or water — on standby (optional)
steps: Prep: Peel and slice the swede and potatoes to the same size, and dice the onion.
Fry the bacon: Fry the cubed bacon in a little butter, stirring, to render out as much fat as possible. Lift out the bacon and leave the fat in the pan.
Soften the onion: Fry the onion briefly in the bacon fat to release its flavour.

Cook the veg: Add the potatoes and swede, season with a little salt and a good amount of black pepper, and stir-fry slowly, covering with a lid between stirs, until tender. Don't rush it. A splash of stock or water can speed things up, though traditionally none is used.
Crisp it up: Return the bacon, stir it through, and with the lid off turn up the heat to dry out the pan and brown a crust on the bottom.
Serve: Serve with a fried egg or bread. Optional: pack the fry into a buttered loose-bottomed ring, turn it out into a buttered pan, cover and brown the base on a low heat, then turn it onto a plate.

recipes.title: TIPSY Laird TRADITIONAL SCOTTISH Dessert
ingredients: Custard (made from powder per packet instructions, or from a tin)
Madeira cake (or a plain pound cake)
Scotch whisky — 6–7 tbsp (or juice for an alcohol-free version)
steps: Make the custard: Make the custard and let it cool.
Toast the almonds: Dry-toast the flaked almonds in a pan and set aside for the garnish.
Jam the cake: Slice the Madeira cake, spread it with raspberry jam, and lay it in the base of the trifle dish. Break up the remaining cake.
Soak: Spoon whisky over the cake, about 6–7 tbsp in total, pressing in the broken cake and adding more whisky between layers.
Add raspberries: Dot on a little more jam, then a layer of fresh raspberries, squashing them in slightly.
Add the custard: Pour the cooled custard over and chill for about half an hour to firm up slightly.
Add the cream: Whip the cream with a little sugar and spread it over the custard.
Decorate: Top with fresh raspberries, toasted almonds, and chocolate sprinkles if using. Chill again before serving.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xQ8stPlm3jQ

recipes.title: BRITISH PANCAKES
ingredients: Melted butter — a little, plus butter for the pan
steps: Make the batter: Stir the flour and salt together, beat in the 2 eggs, then add the milk and whisk until lump-free and frothy (no need to sieve).
Add butter and rest: Stir in a little melted butter, then let the batter stand for 20 minutes so the flour absorbs the liquid for tender pancakes.
Cook: Heat a little butter in a pan over a medium flame. Pour in a little batter and swirl to coat the pan thinly. The first pancake is usually the worst.
Flip: When the pancake moves freely as you shake the pan, flip it (toss it, turn it with a slice, or slide it to the edge and turn it over). Cook a minute or two more until lightly browned.
Repeat: Add a little butter before each pancake.
Serve: Sprinkle with a little sugar and lemon juice, roll up, and drizzle with golden syrup, with a slice of lemon.

From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MFlj9d7endY

recipes.title: Madeira Cake CLASSIC BRITISH sponge cake
ingredients: Butter or margarine, plus extra for greasing
steps: Prep the tin: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F); the air fryer oven in the video uses 165°C. Butter a 2 lb loaf tin (about 12.5 × 23 cm, 8 cm deep) and line it with parchment, leaving overhanging ends for lifting out.
Cream: Cream the butter or margarine with the sugar (it needn't go pale), then mix in about 1 tbsp lemon juice and the lemon zest.
Mix the flours: Combine the self-raising and plain flour with a little salt.
Add the eggs: Add all the eggs at once with a spoonful of the flour to stop curdling and beat in. Scrape down the bowl, then beat in about half the remaining flour.
Finish the batter: Add a splash of milk and fold in the rest of the flour until fully incorporated, without overbeating.
Fill the tin: Spoon the batter into the tin, push it into the corners with a stabbing motion, smooth the top, and tap the tin.
Bake: Bake for 40–45 minutes and test with a skewer. If it isn't done, cover with foil and bake for about 8 minutes more until the skewer comes out clean.
Cool: Leave in the tin for about 5–8 minutes, then lift out using the paper and slice.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cdGdmQ4wzz0

recipes.title: CORNISH  PASTY  Traditional BRITISH pastry CORNWALL  @HYSapientia
ingredients: Water with a little apple cider vinegar
Beef (skirt or chuck; topside in the video), cut into small cubes
Potato, peeled and cut into small cubes
Swede (rutabaga), peeled and cut into small cubes
Egg — 1, beaten with a little milk
steps: Make the pastry: Rub the shortening and butter into the flour and salt with your fingertips until it looks like breadcrumbs. Beat the egg into the water and vinegar, stir it in with a fork handle, then bring together by hand into a crumbly, workable dough. Split it in two (freeze or chill the spare half), flatten into a disc, wrap and chill for about 10 minutes.
Mix the filling: Combine the finely diced onion, potato, swede and beef in a bowl, season with salt and white pepper, and toss. It will start to release some liquid.
Make the glaze: Beat an egg with a little milk.

Shape: Roll the pastry, not too thin, and cut rounds of at least 22 cm (the video uses a pie tin as a guide). Pile filling slightly off centre, brush the edge with glaze, fold over, press to seal, and fold and crimp the edge into a crust. Make a couple of vent holes.
Glaze: Place the pasties on a tray and brush all over with the egg and milk wash.
Bake: Bake in a preheated oven at about 180°C (350°F), or 165°C in the video's air fryer oven, for about 35–40 minutes until golden and cooked through. Cool briefly before eating.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IowlfAXoFJQ
Uploaded 2024-02-10.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 180°C (360°F/Gas 6). 35 – 40 mins; Air fryer 165°C (330°F) 35 mins.

recipes.title: DUNDEE Cake  TRADITIONAL Scottish fruit cake AIR FRYER @HYSapientia
ingredients: Scotch whisky (or orange juice) — a splash for the batter
Marmalade — some for the batter, plus more to glaze
Dried fruit, soaked for about 4 hours in black tea and Scotch whisky, then drained
steps: Cream: Cream the butter and sugar until combined and a little light.
Add the eggs: Add all the eggs with a little flour to stop curdling and mix in. Stir in the ground almonds.
Add the flour: Mix in the self-raising flour and a pinch of salt, scraping down the bowl.
Add the flavours: Stir in a splash of whisky, some marmalade, the mixed peel and mixed spice, then the orange zest (zest over the top to avoid pith).
Add the fruit: Fold in the cherries and the drained, plumped soaked fruit.

Fill the tin: Preheat the oven to 150°C (300°F); the video uses its air fryer oven's 140°C bake setting on low fan. Spoon the batter into a deep 8-inch tin lined on the base and sides, tap it, and smooth the top.
Decorate: Arrange blanched almonds in concentric rings on top, with a few in the middle.
Bake: Bake for about 1½–1¾ hours until a skewer comes out clean. In the video, after 60 minutes it was covered with foil for another 20 minutes, then baked about 20 minutes more at 160°C.
Glaze: Cool for about 5 minutes, turn out, and brush the top with marmalade. Ideally wrap and leave for 2–3 days before cutting.

recipes.title: RAG Pudding TRADITIONAL  BRITISH LANCASHIRE Dish
ingredients: Suet pastry (about 504 g, four portions of about 126 g):
Cold water — just enough to bind
Minced beef — 450 g (about 112 g per pudding)
Salt and plenty of black pepper
Thick gravy — a little (optional, a modern touch)
Cotton cloths, wetted, plus flour for dusting
steps: Make the pastry: Rub the suet into the self-raising flour and salt until it looks like fine breadcrumbs, then add a little water at a time and bring together into a firm (not soggy) dough without overworking. Divide into four equal portions (about 126 g each).
Mix the filling: Mix the minced beef and onion with salt, plenty of pepper, a good pinch of thyme, a dash of Worcestershire sauce and a little thick gravy if using. Divide into four.
Roll: Roll or press each piece of pastry into a rough circle on a floured surface.

Wrap in cloth: Flour a wet cloth well, lay a pastry round on it, and add a portion of filling. Bring the pastry up around the filling and pinch it together at the top, dust the top with flour, then gather the cloth and tie it off with string into a parcel. Repeat.
Simmer: Lower the parcels into a pan of boiling water, making sure they're fully submerged (a trivet on top helps). Cover, return to the boil, then simmer, not a full boil, for 1½ hours.
Serve: Lift out, unwrap and serve with vegetables. Optional: 10 minutes in the oven firms and crisps the outside.

recipes.title: TEESSIDE Chicken PARMO is the BEST!
ingredients: Butter — a little, for under the chicken
Spanish smoked paprika (or seasoning of choice)
steps: Flatten: Put the chicken breasts in a bag and bash them to an even thickness (or butterfly them).
Season: Season the chicken itself on both sides with a little salt and pepper.
Bread: Coat in flour, dip in egg, and press into breadcrumbs, sprinkling Parmesan on. Double-dip: back into the egg, then breadcrumbs with more Parmesan and the bacon bits, patting the crumbs on.
Fry: Shallow-fry in hot oil, laying the chicken away from you, turning until golden on both sides and cooked through. Drain.

Make the béchamel: Warm the milk with a little pepper, whisk in cornflour, add a little Parmesan, and stir until it thickens like custard. Stir in a small knob of butter and cook a little longer so it's thick enough to cling.
Top: Put a little butter on a tray and sit the chicken on it. Spread over the béchamel, then add bacon bits, Parmesan, mozzarella, smoked paprika and a few more bacon bits.
Bake: Bake or grill at about 170–180°C (340–350°F) for a few minutes until the cheese is melted and browned to your liking. Serve with chips, wedges or salad.

recipes.title: LEMON Drizzle classic BRITISH Cake
ingredients: Butter or margarine, plus a little for greasing
steps: Prep the tin: Grease a 2 lb loaf tin and line it with parchment (or a cake liner). Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F); the video's air fryer oven uses 165°C.
Zest and juice: Zest one lemon, zesting over the top to avoid the pith, then juice both lemons.
Cream: Cream the butter or margarine with the sugar, then mix in the lemon zest.
Add the eggs: Beat in the 4 eggs with a couple of tablespoons of the flour to stop curdling.
Add the flour: Beat in just over half the remaining flour, then the rest, scraping down the bowl until fully incorporated.
Bake: Spoon into the tin, smooth gently, and tap. Bake for about 40–50 minutes (about 40 minutes in the video's air fryer oven), until a skewer comes out clean.
Make the icing: Stir a couple of tablespoons of the lemon juice into the icing sugar to make a glaze.
Drizzle: Rest the cake 5 minutes, lift it onto a rack over a tray, and poke holes over the top away from the edges. Spoon over the remaining lemon juice, re-pouring any that runs off.
Ice: Pour the icing over so it runs down the sides, and sprinkle with a little lemon zest. Cool for about 5 minutes before slicing.

recipes.title: Bread Pudding CLASSIC DESSERT NOT Bread and Butter
ingredients: Day-old bread (sliced is fine), crusts on — about 4 cups, torn
Evaporated milk (or milk or cream) — enough to make it soggy
Sugar, plus a little for the top
steps: Soak the bread: Tear the bread into a bowl, pour over the evaporated milk, and turn it over until soggy, adding more liquid if it looks dry.
Mix the custard: Beat the eggs with about 1 tsp vanilla, then add a little salt, nutmeg, cinnamon, the raisins and sugar.
Combine: Stir the egg mixture through the soaked bread.

Fill the dish: Preheat the oven to 175°C (350°F); the video's air fryer oven uses 160°C. Butter a dish and spoon in the mixture loosely, leaving peaks so they brown and crisp. Sprinkle with a little sugar.

recipes.title: Bara Brith TRADITIONAL WELSH Tea Bread
ingredients: Currants and a few sultanas, soaked in cold strong tea (2 tea bags in a cup of water) until plump
Extra cold tea — to loosen the batter
steps: Soak the fruit: Brew 2 tea bags in a cup of water and let it go completely cold. Pour it over the currants and sultanas and leave until the fruit has absorbed the tea and plumped up.
Mix the dry ingredients: Stir together the self-raising flour, about 1 tbsp mixed spice, brown sugar and a little salt.
Make the batter: Stir in the fruit with any remaining tea and the beaten egg, then add more tea until you have a thick but pourable batter.
Fill the tin: Preheat the oven to 170°C (340°F). Pour the batter into a lined 2 lb loaf tin; no need to smooth it.
Bake: Bake for about 60 minutes (50 minutes at 150°C in the video's air fryer oven), covering with foil if it browns too fast, until a skewer comes out clean.
Soften the crust: Brush or rub butter over the hot top right away. After about 5 minutes, turn out onto a rack. If the crust is too hard, put the cooled loaf in a bag or container to soften.
Serve: Slice and serve with butter (or sharp cheddar) and a pot of tea.

recipes.title: Traditional WELSH Corned Beef Rissoles
ingredients: Mashed potato (plain, no butter or milk)
Black pepper (no added salt, as the corned beef is salty)
Plain flour — a little, only if the mix is too wet
Paprika — a little, stirred into the breadcrumbs
steps: Sweat the leek: Finely dice the leek and cook it in a little butter just until soft (browning isn't the aim).
Mix: Combine the plain mash, the leek, black pepper, the corned beef broken into pieces, and the chopped parsley until evenly mixed.
Chill: Refrigerate for about half an hour to firm up. If it's still too wet, stir in a little flour.

Coat: Stir a little paprika into the breadcrumbs. Shape the mix into balls about the size of a tennis ball, roll in the breadcrumbs, dip in beaten egg, and coat in crumbs again. Flatten into patties, then double-dip: back into the egg and crumbs, pressing them compact.
Fry: Shallow-fry in hot oil, turning gently as they're soft, until crisp and golden on both sides. The filling is already cooked.
Serve: Serve with gravy and veg or chips.

recipes.title: CONCRETE  CHOCOLATE!  Old School Cake & Pink Custard
ingredients: Water — a splash if the mix is dry, plus a little for brushing
Pink or red food colouring — a couple of drops
steps: Mix: Stir together the flour, cocoa, a pinch of salt and the sugar. Mix in the melted butter, adding a splash of water if it's too dry, until no dry flour remains.

Press into the tin: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F); the video's air fryer oven uses 160°C. Spread the mix gently into a lined 8-inch square tin, working it into the corners without packing it too hard, and smooth the top with a wet spoon. Sprinkle with a little sugar (optional).
Bake: Bake for 20 minutes.
Finish the top: As soon as it comes out, brush the top lightly with water and sprinkle with sugar. Cool, then lift out and cut into squares.

Make the pink custard: In a pan, combine the milk, about 2 tbsp sugar, a big tablespoon of custard powder, a little strawberry flavouring and a couple of drops of colouring. Whisk over the heat until it just thickens, then take it off the heat.
Serve: Serve squares of concrete cake with plenty of pink custard.

recipes.title: YORKSHIRE Parkin TRADITIONAL POPULAR Cake
ingredients: Quick (porridge) oats, most blended briefly and some left whole for texture
Spices: ground ginger and mixed spice
steps: Prep the oats: Blitz most of the oats briefly in a blender (don't turn them to flour), then mix in some unblended oats for texture.
Mix the dry ingredients: Combine the oats with the flour and spices.
Melt: Gently melt the butter, golden syrup, brown sugar and black treacle in a pan over a low flame until combined, then take off the heat.
Combine: Stir the melted mixture into the dry ingredients until fully incorporated, then stir in the milk and the beaten egg.
Bake: Pour into a lined tray and bake on the middle shelf. The video uses its air fryer oven at 140°C on low fan for 40 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
Wrap and wait: Cool a little, wrap in parchment (turning it over so cracks are underneath), and keep wrapped for 3 days so it turns sticky and the flavours meld before cutting.

recipes.title: SHROPSHIRE FIDGET Pie TRADITIONAL ENGLISH savory pie
ingredients: Water with a little apple cider vinegar
Sour apples — 2, peeled, cored and sliced
Pork tenderloin, trimmed and sliced into rounds
steps: Make the pastry: Rub the shortening and butter into the flour and salt until like breadcrumbs. Beat the egg into the water and vinegar, mix it in, and bring together into a dough. Split into two discs (base and lid), wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.
Par-boil the potatoes: Bring the whole peeled potatoes to the boil and boil for 7 minutes, then slice them into fairly thick slices.
Poach the pork: Bring the cider to the boil with the sliced pork tenderloin and poach until 60–80% cooked. Lift out the pork.
Thicken the cider: Stir about 1 tbsp cornflour into the cider and pork juices until slightly thickened. Set aside.
Line the tin: Line the base of an 8-inch springform tin with parchment. Roll out one pastry disc on a floured surface and line the tin, leaving an overhang.
Layer: Layer potato, apple, onion and pork, then more potato, onion and apple, adding fresh sage, black pepper and a little salt. Finish with apples on top, pouring in the thickened cider as you go.
Top: Roll out the lid, lay it over, fold the overhang over the top, trim the excess, and press it into the tin. Crimp with your fingers, brush with egg wash, and cut several steam vents.
Bake: Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 35 minutes until golden. Cool for about 10 minutes before releasing the ring.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tusBvsZWaVk

recipes.title: GLAMORGAN sausages  Selsig Morgannwg TRADITIONAL WELSH sausage
ingredients: Leeks, cleaned and very thinly sliced (white and pale green)
Caerphilly cheese, grated (some kept back for the sauce)
Dried breadcrumbs (such as panko), plus more for coating
Fresh parsley, finely chopped (some kept back for the sauce)
steps: Cook the leeks: Fry about three-quarters of the sliced leeks gently in a little butter to soften without browning. Turn off the heat, stir in the remaining raw leeks for crunch, and let cool.

Mix: Combine the breadcrumbs, grated Caerphilly, white pepper, about ½ tsp mustard powder and some parsley. Stir in the leeks and the beaten egg, then add milk a splash at a time until the mix just holds together when pressed.
Shape: Roll into sausages of roughly equal size.
Coat: Dip each in beaten egg, then roll in breadcrumbs. Double-dip if you like.
Fry: Shallow-fry in hot oil over a low-moderate flame without crowding, turning gently, until golden and crisp all over. Drain.

Make the sauce: Warm milk with cornflour and white pepper, whisking until it begins to thicken. Add a knob of butter and the reserved cheese, stir until smooth, then take off the heat and stir in parsley and a little mustard if you like.
Serve: Serve the sausages with the cheese sauce, mashed potatoes and veg.

recipes.title: Mince and Crispy Dumplings NO SUET
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
steps: Cook the base: Fry the onion in oil, then add the carrot, celery and a decent pinch of thyme. Add the mince and break it up, season with salt and pepper, and add about 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce. Stir-fry until the mince is cooked through.
Add tomato and gravy: Stir in a good tbsp of tomato purée, then the gravy, and simmer, stirring, until slightly thickened. Use a cornflour slurry only if needed. Turn off the heat.

Make the dumpling dough: Mix the self-raising flour with a little baking powder and salt, then rub in the vegetable shortening until it looks like fine breadcrumbs. Stir in the parsley. Beat the egg into the milk and stir it in just until no dry flour shows. It will be wet and sticky, which is right.

Assemble: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F); the video's air fryer oven uses 170°C. Spoon the mince into a baking dish (about 11 × 7 inches), keeping some gravy aside for serving, then dot spoonfuls of dumpling dough over the top.
Bake: Set the dish on a tray and bake for 20 minutes until the dumplings are risen and crisp on top. Serve with the reserved gravy.

recipes.title: OLD SCHOOL Jam & Coconut Sponge  British Classic
steps: Cream: Beat the butter and sugar for about a minute until light, then add about 1 tsp vanilla.
Add the eggs: Beat in the 4 eggs and a pinch of salt.
Add the flour: Mix in the self-raising flour on a slow speed, add a couple of tablespoons of milk, scrape down the bowl, and give it a quick final blend.
Fill the tin: Pour into a lined 11 × 7-inch tin and spread it evenly into the corners.
Bake: Bake on the middle shelf of a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for about 20 minutes (about 25 minutes at 160°C in the video's air fryer oven), until a skewer comes out clean.
Level and flip: Cool a little, slice off any domed top, then turn the sponge out so the flat bottom is now the top.
Finish: Spread generously with jam and cover with desiccated coconut.
Serve: Cut into squares and serve with custard.

recipes.title: Old-English Treacle Tart: A Classic Recipe Revived
ingredients: Shortcrust pastry (half the batch for one tart):
Water with a little apple cider vinegar
Fresh breadcrumbs — about 150 g (6–8 slices of day-old bread, blitzed)
Lemon — zest of 1 and about 3 tbsp juice
Egg — 1, beaten (a little used to seal the case)
steps: Make the pastry: Rub the shortening and butter into the flour and salt until like breadcrumbs. Mix in the egg beaten into the water and vinegar, and bring together. Split into two discs, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes (freeze the spare).
Make breadcrumbs: Blitz about 150 g of day-old bread into fresh crumbs. Dry crumbs work but need longer to soak.

Line and blind bake: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F); the video's air fryer oven uses 170°C. Line the base of a 9-inch loose-bottom tin with parchment, roll out the pastry, and line the tin, leaving a slight overhang. Prick the base, fill with parchment and baking beads, and bake for 15 minutes.
Seal: Remove the beads, brush the base with some of the beaten egg, and bake for no more than 2 minutes. Cool, then trim the overhang.

Make the filling: Gently melt butter in a pan, then stir in the golden syrup, 1–2 tbsp black treacle and a pinch of salt without boiling. Add the lemon zest and about 3 tbsp juice, turn off the heat, and stir in the breadcrumbs. Let it cool.
Add the egg: Mix the rest of the beaten egg with about 3 tbsp milk and stir it into the cooled filling (if it's still hot, the egg will scramble).
Bake: Spoon the filling into the case and level it. Reduce the oven to 150°C (300°F) and bake for about 15–20 minutes until set.
Serve: Cool a little and serve warm with vanilla ice cream or custard, or eat cold.

recipes.title: Yorkshire FAT RASCALS a delightful BRITISH treat
ingredients: Almonds — to blanch (or ready-blanched), 3 per rascal
Buttermilk (or milk soured with a little vinegar for 5 minutes)
steps: Blanch the almonds: Cover the almonds with boiling water for a minute, move them to cold water, then rub or peel off the skins.
Cream: Cream the butter and brown sugar together, then mix in about 1 tsp mixed spice and the orange zest.
Make the dough: Stir in the plain flour, self-raising flour and baking soda, then the eggs and buttermilk, to form a dough. Mix in the dried fruit with a spoon. The dough should be fairly firm.
Shape: Weigh the dough and divide it into six (about 160 g each). Shape into rough rounds on a parchment-lined tray without squashing them much.
Decorate: Press on two halved glacé cherries for eyes and three blanched almonds for a smile, then brush with egg wash.

Bake: Bake on the middle shelf of an oven at about 200°C (400°F) for about 20 minutes. In the video's air fryer oven at 170°C, 20 minutes was a little too long and 12 was used for the next batch. Cool briefly before eating.

recipes.title: Cake and Chips TRADITIONAL YORKSHIRE Style
ingredients: Large potatoes, peeled (some cut into chips, some into slices under 1 cm thick)
Ground rice (rice cones, not rice flour)
steps: Blanch the chips: Cut the potatoes into chips and fry at 140°C for 4–6 minutes only, shaking the basket so they don't stick, until barely coloured. Drain and set aside.
Make the batter: Whisk the flour with water and baking soda to the consistency of single cream. Set aside.
Slice: Cut large potatoes into slices no thicker than 1 cm, so they cook through.

Build the cakes: Dip one side of a potato slice in ground rice, pile fish pieces on that side, then top with a second slice, ground-rice side inward. Roll the whole cake in ground rice, edges and faces, to absorb moisture and help the batter stick.

Batter and fry: Stir a splash of vinegar into the batter so it fizzes. Dip each cake, pinching the batter around the edges, and lower it into oil at 180°C. Hold it down and turn it as it puffs up, frying until a knife slides easily through the potato. Drain.
Save the scraps: Scoop out the crispy batter bits (scraps) for serving.
Finish the chips: Fry the blanched chips at 180°C for about 3 minutes, shaking, until crisp. Drain.
Serve: Serve the cakes with chips and scraps, plenty of salt and vinegar.

recipes.title: OLD SCHOOL CHOCOLATE Sponge and PINK Custard  CLASSIC UK school dessert
ingredients: Cornflour/cornstarch — a couple of heaped tbsp
Pink or red food colouring — a little
steps: Make the batter: Cream the butter and sugar. Beat in the eggs with a pinch of salt and a little vanilla, then the milk. Mix the self-raising flour and cocoa, sift it into the wet mix, and mix slowly, then fold until fully incorporated.

recipes.title: Cock-a-Leekie Soup Recipe TRADITIONAL SCOTTISH DISH
ingredients: Chicken legs, skin on and bone in
Chicken stock (or chicken cooking water), plus extra water as needed
Celery, cut into roughly 1 cm pieces
Leeks — 3: 2 in large chunks (some green included), 1 sliced fairly thin
steps: Start the chicken: Put the chicken legs in a wide pan with the chicken stock and water, bring to the boil, and skim off any foam.
Prep the veg: Dice the onion, cut the celery and carrots into chunks, and cut two leeks into fairly large chunks. Slice the third leek thinly and set it aside.

Simmer: Add the veg, a little more water if needed, the peppercorns, about 1 tsp thyme, the bay leaves, prunes and pearl barley. Cover and simmer for about an hour, until the barley is tender and the broth has thickened. The video plans to add the thinly sliced leek for the last 15 minutes or so (in the end it goes in with the rest).
Shred the chicken: Turn off the heat, lift out the chicken, and shred the meat with two forks, discarding the skin and bones. Return the meat to the pan.
Finish: Taste and add salt, remove the bay leaves, and simmer for about 10 minutes more so the leeks soften but keep some texture. Serve hot.

recipes.title: Ham at home in 48 hours  Boiled or Roasted
ingredients: Brine (from the description: 2 litres / 4 litres batch):
Chilli flakes — 2 tbsp (dried red chillies were used)
Pork loin and other boneless pork pieces (about 980 g and 1,031 g pieces were used)
Honey mustard, brown sugar and whisky glaze:
2 tbsp whisky (Irish whiskey was used; bourbon works)
1 tsp ground cinnamon (optional; about ½ tsp was used)
½ tsp ground cloves (optional; about ¼ tsp was used)
steps: Make the brine: Combine the water, salt, sugar, pink curing salt and all the spices, bring to the boil and boil about 20 minutes until everything dissolves. Let it cool completely.

Weigh and inject: Weigh each piece of pork and calculate 10% of its weight (e.g. 98 g of brine for a 980 g piece). Draw that much cooled brine (without the spices) into a meat injector and inject it all over the meat in as many places as possible.

Bag and cure: Put each piece in a zip bag, divide the remaining brine between the bags with a few of the whole spices (leave out the star anise and cinnamon sticks so they don't puncture the bag), squeeze out the air, seal and double-bag. Refrigerate 48 hours, turning the bags every 4–5 hours or so when you can.

Rinse and dry: Remove the pork from the bags and rinse well under the tap; if you are worried about saltiness, soak it covered in water about 6 hours. Pat dry, set on a rack over a tray and air-dry in the fridge about 6 hours or overnight.

Boiled ham: Put the ham in a pan of water with a probe thermometer set to 71°C, bring to the boil, then turn down to a gentle simmer (not a rolling boil, which toughens it) for about 45–50 minutes, until it reaches 71°C. Turn off and let it stand 15 minutes.

Make the glaze: Gently heat the brown sugar, honey, mustard, vinegar, cinnamon, cloves and whisky until the sugar dissolves and it just comes to the boil. Turn off and cool; keep it brushable rather than too thick.

Roast ham: Heat the oven to about 160°C. Lightly score the fat (optional) and roast the ham about 45 minutes, until it reaches 71°C inside. About 15–20 minutes before the end, spoon or brush on the glaze (from a separate bowl to avoid contaminating the pan), and repeat once more.
Glazed boiled ham (optional): Brush glaze over a boiled ham and roast at 200°C for 6–7 minutes to crisp the top.
Cool and slice: Let the hams cool, then slice. The description notes the ham keeps 7–10 days refrigerated when tightly wrapped, or up to 6 months frozen when airtight.
